sweep:model-anchors.summary: Full property inventory of the FDAT-relevant LCM classes from MasterLCModel.xml (model version 7000072), with answers to the four questions. Key results: (1) A Text CAN hold many media files: Text.MediaFiles (OA, CmMediaContainer) -> CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs (OC, CmMediaURI); each CmMediaURI stores a single Unicode string 'MediaURI' (a media-fragment URI, ELAN placeholder) plus the container's Unicode 'OffsetType' - it does NOT reference a CmFile and FLEx only writes it from BIRD/ELAN import. The separate LinkedFiles machinery (CmFile.InternalPath/OriginalPath, owned by CmFolder under LangProject.Media/Pictures/FilePathsInTsStrings) is what FLExBridge syncs (LinkedFiles/AudioVisual|Others|Pictures/**.*). (2) Free/rich-text slots: Text.Source (MultiString), Text.Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), inherited Name (MultiUnicode) and Description (MultiString); StText has none itself; StTxtPara.Contents/Label (String); Segment.FreeTranslation/LiteralTranslation (MultiString), Reference (String), BeginTimeOffset/EndTimeOffset (Unicode), Notes (OS Note, Note.Content MultiString); ConstChartRow.Notes and .Label (String); CmPossibility.Name/Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), Description (MultiString), Discussion (OA StText), HelpId (Unicode); RnGenericRec.Title (String) plus many OA StText fields. (3) Possibility references: Text.Genres (RC), ConstituentChartCellPart.Column (RA), ConstChartTag.Tag (RA), TextTag.Tag (RA), DsChart.Template (RA), CmPossibility.Restrictions (RC)/Confidence (RA)/Status (RA), Segment.Speaker (RA CmPerson), RnGenericRec.Confidence/Restrictions/PhraseTags/TimeOfEvent/Type/Status, CmTranslation.Type, and LCM custom ReferenceAtomic/ReferenceCollection fields with DstCls=CmPossibility. (4) Open fields: ConstChartRow has Notes(String)+Label(String); Segment has Notes(OS Note), Reference(String), and is one of the six classes FLEx's UI allows custom fields on; StTxtPara has Label(String, unused); CmPossibility has Description, Discussion(StText), HelpId, plus ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor/UnderStyle/Hidden integers/booleans usable for colour. The model XML has NO attribute marking custom-field-capable classes; LCM's AddCustomField accepts any model class; FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog restricts the UI to LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm, Segment, RnGenericRec.

findings.claim: Text (num 54, base CmMajorObject, owner="none") has exactly these own properties: Source (MultiString), Contents (owning atomic StText), Genres (reference collection CmPossibility), Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), IsTranslated (Boolean), MediaFiles (owning atomic CmMediaContainer); it inherits Name (MultiUnicode), DateCreated/DateModified (Time), Description (MultiString), Publications (OC Publication), HeaderFooterSets (OC PubHFSet) from CmMajorObject.
findings.evidence: <basic num="2" id="Source" sig="MultiString"/> <owning num="8" id="Contents" card="atomic" sig="StText"/> <rel num="9" id="Genres" card="col" sig="CmPossibility"/> <basic num="10" id="Abbreviation" sig="MultiUnicode"/> <basic num="11" id="IsTranslated" sig="Boolean"/> <owning num="12" id="MediaFiles" card="atomic" sig="CmMediaContainer"> 'A container for media files which are associated with this text, and possibly referenced by segments in the text.' CmMajorObject: Name MultiUnicode, DateCreated, DateModified, Description MultiString, Publications, HeaderFooterSets.
findings.implication: Per-text FDAT anchors exist: Text.Description (MultiString, rich text) and Text.Source are free text; MediaFiles is a single container but it owns a collection, so 'more than one media file' is possible (see next finding). Text is unowned (owner="none"), so it is a top-level object in the FLExBridge TextCorpus files.

findings.claim: A Text CAN hold more than one media/linked file, via Text.MediaFiles (OA, one CmMediaContainer) -> CmMediaContainer.MediaURIs (owning COLLECTION of CmMediaURI). CmMediaContainer stores only OffsetType (Unicode) plus the collection; CmMediaURI stores only a single Unicode string 'MediaURI' described as 'the location and offset of the media file, this should be a subset of the MediaFragment specification'. Neither class references a CmFile or the LinkedFiles folder; both are documented as 'Currently a placeholder for ELAN data, not modifiable or viewable in flex as of Nov 2011'.
findings.evidence: CmMediaURI (num 72): <basic num="1" id="MediaURI" sig="Unicode"> 'The location and offset of the media file, this should be a subset of the MediaFragment specification. see http://www.w3.org/2008/WebVideo/Fragments/WD-media-fragments-spec/'. CmMediaContainer (num 73): 'This class collects any number of MediaURIs and provides an offset type' — <basic num="1" id="OffsetType" sig="Unicode"/> <owning num="2" id="MediaURIs" card="col" sig="CmMediaURI"/>. Segment.MediaURI (rel atomic CmMediaURI, 'This references a media file in the interlinear text').
findings.implication: The owner's 'linked file of the text' idea maps to CmMediaURI, which is just a URI string - it does not copy anything into LinkedFiles, is not shown/edited in FLEx, and FLEx code only writes it during BIRD/ELAN (.flextext) import (BIRDInterlinearImporter.cs:1372-1392 creates the container and adds ICmMediaURI objects by GUID; InterlinearExporter.cs:884-889 exports them). An FDAT JSON could be pointed at by an extra CmMediaURI (MediaURI = relative path under LinkedFiles/Others), but the file itself must be placed in LinkedFiles/Others (or AudioVisual) for FLExBridge to sync it (FlexFolderSystem.cs:61-63 includes only LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, Others, Pictures). InterlinVc.cs:1138 and InterlinDocForAnalysis.cs:2237 read segment.MediaURIRA?.MediaURI for playback, so a Segment pointing at a JSON would be nonsense; a text-level URI not referenced by any Segment is inert. INFERRED: risk that a future FLEx version tries to open all MediaURIs as audio.

findings.claim: The 'real' linked-file model is CmFile (Name MultiUnicode, Description MultiString, OriginalPath Unicode, InternalPath Unicode, Copyright MultiString) owned by CmFolder (Name MultiUnicode, SubFolders OC CmFolder, Description MultiString, Files OC CmFile); LangProject owns three CmFolder roots: Pictures (OC CmFolder), Media (OC CmFolder, 'one CmFolder called Local Media that holds all media'), FilePathsInTsStrings (OA CmFolder, 'holds all externalLink's to files found in TsStrings'); CmPicture.PictureFile and CmMedia.MediaFile are RA CmFile. LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir (Unicode) holds the root path; liblcm hard-codes subfolders LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, /Pictures, /Others.
findings.evidence: CmFile: <basic num="3" id="OriginalPath" sig="Unicode"/> <basic num="4" id="InternalPath" sig="Unicode"/>. CmFolder: <owning num="6" id="Files" card="col" sig="CmFile"/>. LangProject: <owning num="48" id="Pictures" card="col" sig="CmFolder"/> <owning num="51" id="Media" card="col" sig="CmFolder"/> <owning num="56" id="FilePathsInTsStrings" card="atomic" sig="CmFolder"/> <basic num="42" id="LinkedFilesRootDir" sig="Unicode"/>. LcmFileHelper.cs: ksLinkedFilesDir = "LinkedFiles"; ksMediaDir = "AudioVisual"; ksPicturesDir = "Pictures"; ksOtherLinkedFilesDir = "Others".
findings.implication: If FDAT wants a synced sidecar file, the model-sanctioned route is a CmFile (InternalPath relative to LinkedFiles, e.g. Others/<textguid>.fdat.json) registered in a CmFolder under LangProject.Media or FilePathsInTsStrings, and the bytes placed under LinkedFiles/Others which FLExBridge includes (flexbridge FlexFolderSystem.cs:62). Nothing in the model links a CmFile to a Text directly; CmMedia (Label MultiString + MediaFile RA CmFile) is owned only by LexPronunciation.MediaFiles (:2888), so a text->file link would have to go through a custom field or a CmMediaURI string.

findings.claim: StText (num 14) has only: Paragraphs (owning seq StPara), RightToLeft (Boolean), Tags (owning col TextTag), DateModified (Time). It has no free-text, note, or description property of its own.
findings.evidence: <owning num="1" id="Paragraphs" card="seq" sig="StPara"/> <basic num="2" id="RightToLeft" sig="Boolean"> <owning num="3" id="Tags" sig="TextTag" card="col"/> <basic num="4" id="DateModified" sig="Time"/>
findings.implication: StText is the object DsConstChart.BasedOn points at (:4902) and the owner of TextTags; it offers no writable slot for FDAT data, so per-text data must go on the owning Text or on a custom field elsewhere.

findings.claim: StPara (abstract) has StyleRules (TextPropBinary). StTxtPara (num 16) has: Label (String, 'not currently used'), Contents (String, the paragraph text with embedded formatting), ParseIsCurrent (Boolean), TextObjects (ref seq CmObject), AnalyzedTextObjects (owning seq CmObject), Segments (owning seq Segment), Translations (owning col CmTranslation). CmTranslation has Translation (MultiString), Type (RA CmPossibility), Status (MultiUnicode).

findings.implication: StTxtPara.Label is an unused String slot, but writing to it would be a misuse (FLEx may display it in future); Contents must not be touched (editing it invalidates parse/segments). Not a good FDAT anchor.

findings.claim: Segment (num 6) properties: BeginOffset (Integer, internalSetter), FreeTranslation (MultiString), LiteralTranslation (MultiString), Notes (owning seq Note; Note.Content is MultiString), Analyses (ref seq IAnalysis), Reference (String, 'user specified reference for a segment... displayed in the Ref column in the Concordance view... can not be specified in FLEx, but can be imported'), MediaURI (RA CmMediaURI), BeginTimeOffset (Unicode), EndTimeOffset (Unicode), Speaker (RA CmPerson).

Note: <basic num="1" id="Content" sig="MultiString"/>
findings.implication: Segment offers several 'open' slots: Notes (a sequence of Note objects, each a MultiString - user-visible in interlinear as notes, so FDAT data there would be visible/mergeable but pollutes the linguist's notes), Reference (String not editable in FLEx UI per the comment), and Segment is also one of the six classes FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog exposes (LocationType.Interlinear -> SegmentTags.kClassId, AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:119-121), so a custom Segment field is a legitimate per-clause anchor. Chart rows map to Segments via ConstChartWordGroup.BeginSegment/EndSegment.

findings.claim: TextTag (num 22, owned by StText.Tags) properties: BeginSegment (RA Segment), EndSegment (RA Segment), BeginAnalysisIndex (Integer), EndAnalysisIndex (Integer), Tag (RA CmPossibility). The tags come from LangProject.TextMarkupTags (OA CmPossibilityList: 'Top level Possibilities are major tag categories (Syntax, Semantics, RRG, etc.) The actual tags are their SubPossibilities').
findings.evidence: <rel num="1" id="BeginSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/> <rel num="2" id="EndSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/> <basic num="3" id="BeginAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer"> <basic num="4" id="EndAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer"> <rel num="5" id="Tag" sig="CmPossibility" card="atomic"/>. LangProject: <owning num="55" id="TextMarkupTags" card="atomic" sig="CmPossibilityList">
findings.implication: TextTag is a model-sanctioned way to attach a possibility (e.g. an FDAT 'salience band' item in a new top-level category of TextMarkupTags) to a word range in a Segment - it is what FLEx's Text Tagging tool writes, so items would be visible in FLEx and merged by FLExBridge. No free-text field on TextTag itself.

findings.claim: CmPossibility (num 7) properties: Name (MultiUnicode), Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), Description (MultiString), SubPossibilities (owning seq CmPossibility), SortSpec (Integer), Restrictions (RC CmPossibility), Confidence (RA CmPossibility), Status (RA CmPossibility), DateCreated/DateModified (Time), Discussion (OA StText), Researchers (RC CmPerson), HelpId (Unicode), ForeColor (Integer, 'for overlay functionality'), BackColor (Integer), UnderColor (Integer), UnderStyle (Integer 0-127), Hidden (Boolean), IsProtected (Boolean). CmCustomItem (num 27) is a CmPossibility subclass with NO extra properties, whose purpose is 'to allow users to add custom fields to custom lists without affecting standard lists'; custom lists are unowned (CmPossibilityList owner="optional").
findings.evidence: <basic num="15" id="ForeColor" sig="Integer"> 'ForeColor for overlay functionality.' <basic num="16" id="BackColor" sig="Integer"> <basic num="17" id="UnderColor" sig="Integer"> <basic num="18" id="UnderStyle" sig="Integer" min="0" max="127"> <basic num="19" id="Hidden" sig="Boolean"> <basic num="20" id="IsProtected" sig="Boolean">; <owning num="12" id="Discussion" card="atomic" sig="StText">; CmCustomItem: <props/> with comment 'Purpose is to allow users to add custom fields to custom lists'; CmPossibilityList comment 'Custom Lists are unowned in the model, so owner needs to be optional (FWR-133)'.
findings.implication: Every FLEx list item already carries ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor/UnderStyle/Hidden integers - ideal native slots for FDAT's marker styling and salience-band colours (chart markers under DsDiscourseData.ChartMarkers, template columns under ConstChartTempl, salience items in a custom list). Description (MultiString) and Discussion (StText) are free/rich-text slots for glosses/notes. A custom (unowned) CmPossibilityList of CmCustomItem is the FLEx-blessed place for FDAT's own vocabularies; SubPossibilities allow hierarchy, SortSpec allows ordering.

findings.claim: CmPossibilityList (num 8, base CmMajorObject) properties: Depth (Integer), PreventChoiceAboveLevel (Integer), IsSorted (Boolean), IsClosed (Boolean), PreventDuplicates (Boolean), PreventNodeChoices (Boolean), Possibilities (owning seq CmPossibility), Abbreviation (MultiUnicode), HelpFile (Unicode), UseExtendedFields (Boolean), DisplayOption (Integer 0-2), ItemClsid (Integer, 'the clsid of the items that can be inserted into this list'), IsVernacular (Boolean), WritingSystem (Unicode), WsSelector (Integer), ListVersion (Guid); plus inherited Name/Description/DateCreated/DateModified.
findings.evidence: <basic num="14" id="ItemClsid" sig="Integer"> 'This is the clsid of the items that can be inserted into this list.' <owning num="8" id="Possibilities" card="seq" sig="CmPossibility"/> <basic num="21" id="ListVersion" sig="Guid">
findings.implication: When FDAT creates lists it must set ItemClsid (CmCustomItem for custom lists; the CmPossibility comment at :308-314 says the list editor always uses ItemClsid to create new items). IsClosed/IsSorted control whether users may add or reorder. ListVersion (Guid) can be used by FDAT to detect its own schema version of a list.

findings.claim: DsDiscourseData (num 124, singleton, owned by LangProject.DiscourseData) owns: ConstChartTempl (OA CmPossibilityList - templates; top level = chart template, SubPossibilities = column groups/columns), Charts (OC DsChart), ChartMarkers (OA CmPossibilityList - 'markers that can be inserted into the chart... top-level is several different kinds of markers'). DsChart (abstract, base CmMajorObject) has Template (RA CmPossibility). DsConstChart adds BasedOn (RA StText) and Rows (owning seq ConstChartRow); it inherits Name (MultiUnicode) and Description (MultiString) from CmMajorObject.
findings.evidence: <owning num="1" id="ConstChartTempl" card="atomic" sig="CmPossibilityList"> <owning num="2" id="Charts" card="col" sig="DsChart"> <owning num="3" id="ChartMarkers" card="atomic" sig="CmPossibilityList">; DsChart: <rel num="1" id="Template" card="atomic" sig="CmPossibility">; DsConstChart: <rel num="1" id="BasedOn" card="atomic" sig="StText"> <owning num="2" id="Rows" card="seq" sig="ConstChartRow">; LangProject: <owning num="53" id="DiscourseData" card="atomic" sig="DsDiscourseData">
findings.implication: Chart-level FDAT data (prologue/epilogue, preferences) has a native rich-text slot: DsConstChart.Description (MultiString) - and DsConstChart.Name. Marker styling/order/visibility maps onto the CmPossibility items of ChartMarkers (ForeColor/BackColor/Hidden/SortSpec on each item). FLExBridge stores all charts in one file Linguistics/Discourse/<DiscourseChartFilename> (FlexFolderSystem.cs:77), so chart edits by two users merge at the object level there.

findings.claim: ConstChartRow (num 3 in Ling module) properties: Notes (String), ClauseType (Integer enum Normal/Dependent/Song/Speech), EndParagraph (Boolean), EndSentence (Boolean), StartDependentClauseGroup (Boolean), EndDependentClauseGroup (Boolean), Cells (owning seq ConstituentChartCellPart), Label (String). It has no Description/Comment/Discussion, no possibility references, and no custom-field support in the FLEx UI.
findings.evidence: <basic num="1" id="Notes" sig="String"/> <basic num="2" id="ClauseType" sig="Integer"> ('This is an enum with these values: Normal, Dependent, Song, Speech') <basic num="3" id="EndParagraph" sig="Boolean"/> <basic num="4" id="EndSentence" sig="Boolean"/> <basic num="5" id="StartDependentClauseGroup" sig="Boolean"/> <basic num="6" id="EndDependentClauseGroup" sig="Boolean"/> <owning num="7" id="Cells" sig="ConstituentChartCellPart" card="seq"/> <basic num="8" id="Label" sig="String"/>
findings.implication: The only 'open' slot on a row is Notes (a single-WS TsString) - this is the Notes column the linguist sees and edits in FLEx's chart, so storing FDAT structured data there would collide with user notes. Label is the row number string FLEx computes/rewrites ('1a', '2' ...), so it is not a safe place either. Per-row FDAT data (salience band, custom columns) therefore needs a side structure keyed by the ConstChartRow GUID (e.g. a custom field on the Segment(s) the row covers, a TextTag, or entries in an FDAT-owned list/file).

findings.claim: ConstituentChartCellPart (abstract) has Column (RA CmPossibility, 'Specifically a column identifier'), MergesAfter (Boolean), MergesBefore (Boolean). ConstChartWordGroup adds BeginSegment (RA Segment), EndSegment (RA Segment), BeginAnalysisIndex (Integer), EndAnalysisIndex (Integer). ConstChartMovedTextMarker adds WordGroup (RA ConstChartWordGroup), Preposed (Boolean). ConstChartClauseMarker adds DependentClauses (ref seq ConstChartRow). ConstChartTag adds Tag (RA CmPossibility; null = 'missing' marker; 'The CmPossibilities come from the list of chart tags'). None has a text/notes property.
findings.evidence: <rel num="1" id="Column" sig="CmPossibility" card="atomic"> ... ConstChartWordGroup: <rel num="1" id="BeginSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/> <rel num="2" id="EndSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/> <basic num="3" id="BeginAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer"> <basic num="4" id="EndAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer">; ConstChartMovedTextMarker: <rel num="1" id="WordGroup" sig="ConstChartWordGroup" card="atomic"> <basic num="2" id="Preposed" sig="Boolean"/>; ConstChartClauseMarker: <rel num="1" id="DependentClauses" sig="ConstChartRow" card="seq">; ConstChartTag: <rel num="1" id="Tag" sig="CmPossibility" card="atomic">
findings.implication: FDAT's 'listRef tags' are ConstChartTag.Tag -> items in DsDiscourseData.ChartMarkers; styling/order/visibility of a marker can be stored on that CmPossibility item (ForeColor/BackColor/UnderStyle/Hidden/SortSpec) rather than per chart. Rows map to text via WordGroup.BeginSegment/EndSegment, giving the Segment GUID as a stable secondary key for row-level data.

findings.claim: RnGenericRec (num 4, Notebook) has Title (String) and many owning-atomic StText rich-text fields: VersionHistory, ExternalMaterials, FurtherQuestions, Conclusions, Hypothesis, ResearchPlan, Description, PersonalNotes, Discussion; possibility references Confidence (RA), Restrictions (RC), AnthroCodes (RC CmAnthroItem), PhraseTags (RC), TimeOfEvent (RC), Type (RA), Status (RA), Researchers/Sources (RC CmPerson), Locations (RC CmLocation), Participants (OC RnRoledPartic); record links SubRecords (OS RnGenericRec), SeeAlso/SupersededBy (RC), CounterEvidence/SupportingEvidence (RS), CrossReferences (RC), Reminders (RC); DateCreated/DateModified (Time), DateOfEvent (GenDate); and Text (RA Text: 'A text (suitable for analysis in the Words/Texts tool) that is associated with this record').
findings.evidence: <basic num="1" id="Title" sig="String"> <owning num="13" id="ExternalMaterials" card="atomic" sig="StText"> <owning num="29" id="Description" card="atomic" sig="StText"> <owning num="32" id="Discussion" card="atomic" sig="StText"> <rel num="6" id="Restrictions" card="col" sig="CmPossibility"> <rel num="33" id="Text" card="atomic" sig="Text">
findings.implication: A Notebook record can point at a Text (RnGenericRec.Text) and carries nine StText fields plus custom-field support (AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:122-124), so one record per text is a viable, fully FLExBridge-merged container for FDAT prologue/epilogue and free-form notes, at the cost of appearing in the user's Notebook. Note the model says Text is a reference (RA), so the record does not own the Text.

findings.claim: LangProject (num 1, singleton, unowned) holds: lists PartsOfSpeech, TranslationTags, AnthroList, ConfidenceLevels, Restrictions, Roles, Status, Locations, People, Education, TimeOfDay, AffixCategories, Positions, AnnotationDefs, SemanticDomainList, GenreList, TextMarkupTags (all OA CmPossibilityList), CheckLists (OC CmPossibilityList), Thesaurus (RA CmPossibilityList); Styles (OC StStyle 'for use in the Data Notebook and Lexical database'); Filters (OC CmFilter); Overlays (OC CmOverlay); AnalyzingAgents (OC CmAgent); Annotations (OC CmAnnotation); UserAccounts (OC UserConfigAcct); ActivatedFeatures (OC UserAppFeatAct); Pictures (OC CmFolder); Media (OC CmFolder); FilePathsInTsStrings (OA CmFolder); DiscourseData (OA DsDiscourseData); LexDb, ResearchNotebook, MorphologicalData, PhonologicalData, MsFeatureSystem, PhFeatureSystem, TranslatedScripture; strings EthnologueCode, WorldRegion, MainCountry, FieldWorkLocation, AnalysisWss, CurVernWss, CurAnalysisWss, CurPronunWss, VernWss, LinkedFilesRootDir, HomographWs; inherited DateCreated/DateModified/Description (MultiString). There is NO property holding 'custom lists' - they are unowned objects (CmPossibilityList owner="optional").
findings.evidence: <owning num="23" id="Styles" card="col" sig="StStyle"> <owning num="44" id="Annotations" card="col" sig="CmAnnotation"/> <owning num="48" id="Pictures" card="col" sig="CmFolder"/> <owning num="51" id="Media" card="col" sig="CmFolder"> <owning num="52" id="GenreList" ...> <owning num="53" id="DiscourseData" ...> <owning num="55" id="TextMarkupTags" ...> <basic num="42" id="LinkedFilesRootDir" sig="Unicode">; CmPossibilityList: owner="optional" with comment 'Custom Lists are unowned in the model'.
findings.implication: FDAT-wide preferences could live on LangProject.Description (MultiString, but shared with the project description shown in FLEx - not advisable) or better as items in an unowned custom CmPossibilityList (name/description per item), which FLExBridge syncs as a **.list file (FlexFolderSystem.cs:57). Styles (StStyle) are per-project and also synced (**.style, :58).

findings.claim: StStyle (num 17) properties: Name (Unicode), BasedOn (RA StStyle), Next (RA StStyle), Type (Integer 0-255), Rules (TextPropBinary), IsPublishedTextStyle (Boolean), IsBuiltIn (Boolean), IsModified (Boolean), UserLevel (Integer), Context (Integer), Structure (Integer), Function (Integer), Usage (MultiUnicode 'description of the expected usage of the style').
findings.evidence: <basic num="1" id="Name" sig="Unicode"/> <rel num="2" id="BasedOn" card="atomic" sig="StStyle"/> <basic num="5" id="Rules" sig="TextPropBinary"/> <basic num="7" id="IsBuiltIn" sig="Boolean"> ... <basic num="14" id="Usage" sig="MultiUnicode">
findings.implication: Styles give FDAT a native, synced way to define named colour/font treatments (Rules is a binary TsTextProps blob, set via LCM style services), and character styles could be applied inside ConstChartRow.Notes or Segment notes. Usage is a free MultiUnicode slot. INFERRED: FDAT-created styles should leave IsBuiltIn=false so users can delete them.

findings.claim: The model XML has no attribute or list marking which classes may carry custom fields: the <class> element's XSD attributes are only num, id, abbr, abstract, base, depth, singleton, owner, generateBasicCreateMethod. LCM's LcmMetaDataCache.AddCustomField(className, ...) accepts ANY class name in the model (it only checks CheckClid(className), rejects a name clash with a non-custom field, and allocates flid = clid*1000+500+n). The restriction to specific classes is purely in FLEx's UI: AddCustomFieldDlg offers LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm (Lexicon), Segment (Interlinear), RnGenericRec (Notebook), with types SingleLineText (String or MultiUnicode), MultiparagraphText (OwningAtomic StText), Number (Integer), Date (GenDate), ListRefAtomic/ListRefCollection (ReferenceAtomic/ReferenceCollection with DstCls=CmPossibility and a ListRootId).
findings.evidence: MasterLCModel.xsd:26-32 lists class attributes abbr, abstract, base, depth, singleton, owner, generateBasicCreateMethod (no custom-field flag; grep -i custom in MasterLCModel.xml matches only CmCustomItem and comments). LcmMetaDataCache.cs:920-965: 'CheckClid(className); ... if (m_nameToFlid.TryGetValue(MakeFlidKey(clid, fieldName), out flid) && !IsCustom(flid)) throw ...; flid = (clid*1000) + 500;'. AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:111-125: LexEntryTags/LexSenseTags/LexExampleSentenceTags/MoFormTags; 'case LocationType.Interlinear: ... SegmentTags.kClassId, "Segment"'; RnGenericRecTags. AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:402-434 type mapping.
findings.implication: Technically LCM/flexlibs could add a custom field to ConstChartRow or Text, but FLEx's UI, its BasicCustomPropertyFixer (comment at AddCustomFieldDlg.cs:112,123), FLExBridge's custom-property file handling, and the layout/config system are only exercised for the six UI classes. INFERRED: to stay safe FDAT should confine custom fields to Segment (per clause/row anchor) and RnGenericRec (per text), and use lists/TextTags/Description fields for the rest.

findings.claim: FLExBridge learns custom properties from a single project-level file FLExProject.CustomProperties (<AdditionalFields><CustomField class=... name=...>) and registers them on the named class in its own MetadataCache via AddCustomPropInfo(className, FdoPropertyInfo); the folder configuration includes that file, **.list, **.style, LinkedFiles/AudioVisual|Others|Pictures/**.*, Linguistics/TextCorpus/*.textincorpus and Linguistics/Discourse/<DiscourseChartFilename>, and excludes **.xml, **.flextext, **.zip and video extensions.
findings.evidence: MetadataCache.cs:447-452 'internal void AddCustomPropInfo(string className, FdoPropertyInfo propInfo) { ... _classes[className].AddProperty(propInfo); }'; :492-503 reads FlexBridgeConstants.CustomPropertiesFilename, iterates CustomField elements, className = attribute Class. FlexFolderSystem.cs:34 ExcludePatterns '**.xml'; :24 '**.flextext'; :45 AddExcludedVideoExtensions; :48 'FLExProject.CustomProperties'; :57-58 '**.list', '**.style'; :61-63 LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, Others, Pictures '**.*'; :75 Linguistics/TextCorpus/*.textincorpus; :77 Linguistics/Discourse/DiscourseChartFilename.
findings.implication: A JSON sidecar named *.json under LinkedFiles/Others is matched by the '**.*' include (not by the '**.xml' exclude), so it WOULD be sent/received - but as an opaque file (Chorus binary/large-file handling applies; conflicting edits by two users cannot be merged field-by-field, unlike custom fields, list items, TextTags or Segment notes, which live in the merged .textincorpus/.list/discourse XML). Custom properties on any class name are accepted by the FLExBridge MDC as long as the class exists.

sweep:custom-fields.summary: FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog (Src/xWorks/AddCustomFieldDlg.cs) offers exactly six classes, chosen by area: Lexicon -> LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm ("Allomorph"); Notebook -> RnGenericRec ("Record"); Texts & Words -> Segment. Value types offered: Single-line text (String or MultiUnicode depending on WS selector), Multiparagraph text (OwningAtomic StText), List reference single (ReferenceAtomic CmPossibility) and multiple (ReferenceCollection CmPossibility), Date (GenDate), Number (Integer) - and Segment gets only Single-line text. Text, Wordform, ConstChartRow, CmPossibility, TextTag etc. are NOT offered. However, LCM itself (IFwMetaDataCacheManaged.AddCustomField / LcmMetaDataCache.AddCustomField) accepts ANY class name in the model and any CellarPropertyType; the flid is clid*1000+500+n, and CmObject serialises/deserialises <Custom name=..> elements for Guid, Boolean, Integer, GenDate, Time, Unicode, String, Binary, OwningAtomic/ReferenceAtomic, MultiString/MultiUnicode and all four vector types, on any class. Definitions persist in the .fwdata <AdditionalFields><CustomField class= name= type= destclass= wsSelector= helpString= listRoot= label=/> header; values persist as <Custom name="X"> children of the object's <rt> element. FLExBridge splits the definitions into FLExProject.CustomProperties (merged atomically per class+name; explicitly included first in the Chorus folder config), loads them into its own MetadataCache before validating/merging any data file (skipping unknown class names), keys <Custom> elements by "Custom_<class>_<name>", validates custom properties generically via CmObjectValidator (including inside Linguistics/Discourse/Charting.discourse), and writes values back into the .fwdata on Receive. So custom fields on classes like ConstChartRow or ConstChartWordGroup are technically supported end-to-end by LCM and FLExBridge - but (a) FLEx's dialog will not show or let users delete them (it filters to its combo classes), (b) the FLEx DataTree auto-displays custom fields only for objects edited in a data-entry view (not charts), (c) the FixData BasicCustomPropertyFixer only knows MoForm's subclasses, so an Integer/GenDate custom field on an ABSTRACT class with subclasses (e.g. ConstituentChartCellPart) could leave merged new objects missing the required value element; value-type fields on concrete leaf classes are fine, and reference/string/StText fields are optional elements and unaffected; (d) FLEx itself warns that Send/Receive of custom-field definition CHANGES is fragile and recommends one designated person add fields; (e) FLEx refuses to add fields when another app shares the project. flexlibs offers GetFieldID/GetCustomFieldValue/LexiconSetFieldText/LexiconSetFieldInteger/LexiconSetListField* which take any hvo/object and flid (they are not restricted to lexicon classes despite the names) but supports only String, MultiUnicode/MultiString, Integer and CmPossibility references; it has no wrapper to create custom fields (must call the LCM MDC AddCustomField via pythonnet directly, inside a UOW). Custom Segment/StText/list/reference fields could each carry FDAT data, but the mirror-image design choice remains: a custom field on ConstChartRow is invisible in FLEx UI yet fully synced, whereas a custom field on Segment is user-visible in the interlinear Configure dialog.

Text, WfiWordform, ConstChartRow, CmPossibility, TextTag, StText are NOT offered.

findings.claim: LCM's metadata cache AddCustomField accepts any class name that exists in the model and any CellarPropertyType; the only restrictions are that the class exists, the field name is non-empty, and the name does not collide with a built-in field. It does not restrict to the dialog's classes, nor reject abstract classes. The new flid is clid*1000+500 (+1 per additional custom field on that class).

FDAT should create its fields once (idempotently, checking existence by name first) and never change their type.

This is generic - it works for any class name in the model, including ConstChartRow.

findings.claim: FLEx explicitly warns users that Send/Receive of custom-field DEFINITION changes is only partially supported and can leave team members unable to merge: the dialog shows this warning whenever the project has a FLEx S/R repo, and recommends that a single designated person add fields, that everyone S/R first, and that type changes be done as separate delete-then-add cycles.

FLEx currently has only limited ability to Send/Receive custom field changes. The important thing is to avoid two people adding custom fields with the same name. We recommend that teams agree on one person who will make all custom field changes.' findings.implication: FDAT's field-creation step is the risky S/R moment. Design: create all FDAT custom fields in one go, with fixed names, idempotently (check GetFieldId2 first), never rename/retype; instruct the team that the first user to run FDAT should S/R immediately and others S/R before using FDAT. Adding is 'safe with less trouble'; concurrent additions of the same name by two users is the failure mode.

findings.claim: FLEx refuses to open the custom field dialog when more than one application is connected to the same project (shared backend).

findings.claim: LCM's FixData BasicCustomPropertyFixer (run by FLExBridge/FLEx to repair merged data) adds missing default <Custom name=.. val="0"/> elements for Integer/GenDate custom fields, but maps class -> subclasses only by a hard-coded kludge for MoForm; for any other class with concrete subclasses the fix will not reach the subclasses. The dialog code comments say adding classes with subclasses to the dialog requires changing this fixer.

findings.implication: Avoid Integer/GenDate (value-type) custom fields on abstract classes with subclasses (ConstituentChartCellPart, MoForm-like) and on classes where merges may create instances lacking the value; on concrete leaf classes (ConstChartRow, ConstChartWordGroup, Segment) the fixer handles them by exact class name. Safest: use String/MultiUnicode/ReferenceAtomic/OwningAtomic(StText) types, which are optional elements and need no default. INFERENCE: whether FixData is invoked on the chart file during S/R is not verified here.

findings.claim: Data migrations can collide with custom field names: when a model version adds a built-in field whose name equals an existing custom field on that class, LCM renames or removes the custom field (7000069 did this for LexSense 'UsageNote'/'Exemplar'); a custom field with the same name as a built-in field is refused by AddCustomField.

Rename any Custom Field UsageNote and Exemplar on LexSense to prevent a crash trying to register a Custom Field with the same name as a built-in field.' ... cf.m_fieldname = cfName + nameSuffix;  and '// Don't allow custom field with same name as non-custom field'
findings.implication: Prefix FDAT custom field names distinctively (e.g. 'FDAT_Band', 'FDATData') to avoid future built-in name collisions; migrations otherwise preserve custom fields by class/name (7000066 even back-fills default values for basic custom props).

findings.claim: flexlibs (Python) exposes GetFieldID(className, fieldName) (any class, uses mdc.GetFieldId with base classes), GetCustomFieldValue(objOrHvo, flid) for String, MultiUnicode/MultiString, Integer, ReferenceAtom (returns CmPossibility ShortName) and ReferenceCollection; setters LexiconSetFieldText (String/Multi*), LexiconSetFieldInteger, LexiconClearField, LexiconAddTagToField, LexiconSetListFieldSingle/Multiple. Despite the 'Lexicon' names they take any object or hvo and any flid and go through DomainDataByFlid (ISilDataAccess), so they work on any class; they do not support StText/OwningAtomic, GenDate, or reference fields to non-CmPossibility targets; flexlibs has no API to CREATE custom fields (no AddCustomField/FieldDescription usage).

LexiconGet*CustomFields helpers enumerate only LexEntry/LexSense/LexExampleSentence/MoForm.
findings.implication: FDAT's Python layer can read/write String/MultiUnicode/Integer/list-reference custom fields on ConstChartRow etc. with existing flexlibs calls (passing the row object and a flid from GetFieldID('ConstChartRow','FDATBand')), inside a UOW. To create the fields it must call the LCM MDC directly via pythonnet: IFwMetaDataCacheManaged(project.MetaDataCacheAccessor).AddCustomField(...) - inside an undoable UOW and while no other app is connected - then commit so the AdditionalFields header is written.

findings.claim: The FLExTools GitHub wiki (Home, Customising FlexTools, Technical documentation, v1/v2 pages) contains no page or guidance on custom fields, on the FLExProject custom-field API, or on creating fields; the Technical documentation page only points to LCM model resources. flexlibs' sphinx docs (docs/sphinx/flexlibs.rst) contain no 'custom' mention either.
findings.evidence: WebFetch of https://github.com/cdfarrow/FLExTools/wiki listed pages Home, Customising FlexTools, FLExTools 1to2 Migration Guide, FLExTools v1, FLExTools v2, Technical documentation; Technical-documentation fetch: 'does not contain any information about custom fields, writing to the FLEx project, the FLExProject API'; grep -i custom over flexlibs/docs/sphinx/*.rst returned nothing.
findings.implication: No documented precedent for creating custom fields from FLExTools; FDAT would be relying on the LCM API directly (which is well-defined, per above) rather than a documented flexlibs path. Any lingtransoft/software.sil.org docs could not be checked (blocked).

findings.claim: The Chorus folder configuration for a FLEx repo syncs, besides the split data files, LinkedFiles/AudioVisual/**, LinkedFiles/Others/**, LinkedFiles/Pictures/** and SupportingFiles/**, but excludes **.xml, **.flextext, **.zip, **.log, **.tmp and Temp/**, BackupSettings/** (include list is explicit).
