IncludePatterns.Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "AudioVisual", "**.*")); Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Others", "**.*")); Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "Pictures", "**.*")); Add(Path.Combine("SupportingFiles", "**.*"))
findings.implication: Relevant to the owner's alternative idea: a JSON file placed under LinkedFiles/Others/ would be synced (as an opaque file, no 3-way merge - Chorus binary/LargeFileFilter behaviour not verified here), but a .xml file anywhere would be excluded. Out of scope for this custom-fields investigation but noted.

openQuestions: Whether FLExBridge/FLEx actually runs FwDataFixer (BasicCustomPropertyFixer) over the discourse chart data during Send/Receive, and thus whether an Integer/GenDate custom field on ConstChartRow would be back-filled after a merge that introduces a new row from a user lacking the definition (the fixer keys on exact class name, so concrete classes should be handled; not executed/verified).

Whether a custom OwningAtomic(StText) field on a class outside the dialog's set displays or behaves sensibly (owned StText paragraphs, styles) - LCM serialises it generically but no UI exercises it on e.g. ConstChartRow.

How Chorus handles a JSON/text file under LinkedFiles/Others (LargeFileFilter size cap, text vs binary conflict handling) - the chorus repo was not cloned; needs a separate investigation for the owner's linked-file idea.

Whether SharedXMLBackendProvider (FLEx open concurrently with FDAT/flexlibs) correctly propagates newly-added custom field definitions to the other process, or whether FDAT must require FLEx to be closed when creating fields (FLEx itself refuses the dialog when multiple apps are connected).
Behaviour of LCM data migrations for custom fields on classes that a future model version renames or removes (custom definitions are keyed by class name string).

sweep:linked-files.summary: Linked files are a workable but narrow place for an FDAT JSON. Send/Receive (FLExBridge on Chorus/Mercurial) includes exactly three LinkedFiles subfolders of the project folder — LinkedFiles/AudioVisual, LinkedFiles/Others, LinkedFiles/Pictures (plus SupportingFiles) — via explicit include patterns; nothing else in the project folder is synced unless explicitly listed. ".json" is not excluded (only **.xml, **.zip, and video/backup/temp extensions are), so <project>/LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/<something>.json will be committed and pushed. Constraints that the design depends on: (1) the hg repo root is the folder of the .fwdata file, so the file only syncs when LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir is the default in-project LinkedFiles folder (a project whose LinkedFiles were relocated to a shared drive syncs none of them); (2) Chorus's LargeFileFilter caps unknown extensions such as .json at 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes; images/audio get 10 MiB, .txt/.lift unlimited) — an oversized file is excluded and, if already tracked, 'forgotten' with only a warning in the S/R log; (3) no handler merges .json: FlexBridge's handler declines it and Chorus falls to DefaultFileTypeHandler, which records an 'unmergable file type' conflict note and keeps the merging machine's copy ('WeWin'), i.e. whole-file, last-merger-wins, other side's edits silently dropped from the working copy. At the model level, no LCM property is needed for the file to sync; the properties that can point at a linked file are CmFile.InternalPath (relative to LinkedFilesRootDir, owned in CmFolders under LangProject.Pictures/Media/FilePathsInTsStrings and referenced by CmPicture.PictureFile and CmMedia.MediaFile), kodtExternalPathName runs in TsStrings ('Insert Link to File', which copies the file into LinkedFiles/Others and registers a CmFile), and CmMediaURI.MediaURI (a raw URI string, one Text.MediaFiles container holding any number of CmMediaURIs, created only by FLExText import, shown read-only as static text in the Text's Info tab 'Media' field, played only when a Segment references it and the URI is an existing local file; no type validation). A CmMediaURI pointing at a .json therefore 'works' (FLEx displays the path, never opens it), but it conflates FDAT data with ELAN media metadata that gets exported/re-imported with the text; a CmFile in a dedicated CmFolder under LangProject.Media, or simply no pointer at all, is cleaner. FLEx backup includes everything under an in-project LinkedFiles folder when 'include linked files' is checked, and only CmFile-registered files when LinkedFiles is elsewhere.

findings.claim: FLExBridge syncs only three LinkedFiles subfolders, by explicit include pattern: LinkedFiles/AudioVisual/**.*, LinkedFiles/Others/**.*, LinkedFiles/Pictures/**.* (plus SupportingFiles/**.*). A file anywhere else in the project folder (project root, ConfigurationSettings, LinkedFiles/<other subfolder>) is not synced.
findings.evidence: projectFolderConfiguration.IncludePatterns.Add(Path.Combine("LinkedFiles", "AudioVisual", "**.*")); ... ("LinkedFiles", "Others", "**.*"); ... ("LinkedFiles", "Pictures", "**.*"); ... ("SupportingFiles", "**.*"). Header comment: 'we're using the policy that we explicitly include all the files we understand'.
findings.implication: An FDAT JSON must live under <project>/LinkedFiles/Others (or AudioVisual/Pictures) to be carried by Send/Receive. A subfolder such as LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/ is covered because the pattern is **.* (Mercurial '**' matches across directory separators — inferred from hg glob semantics, not from FLExBridge code).

findings.claim: The complete exclude list does not mention .json. Excluded are: **.fwdata (FwXmlExtension), **.fwdata-replaced, **.fwdata-x, **.fwdb, **.bad, **.bak, **.flextext, **.fwbackup, **.fwstub, **.lint, **.log, **.orig, **.oxekt, **.oxes, **.oxesa, **.tmp, **.xml, **.zip, **.fwdata.lock, **.dupid, Temp/**.*, BackupSettings/**.*, WritingSystemStore/trash/**.*, WritingSystemStore/WritingSystemsToIgnore.xml.ChorusNotes, OtherRepositories/**.*, **.NewChorusNotes, and the video extensions added by ProjectFolderConfiguration.AddExcludedVideoExtensions. Exclude patterns take precedence over include patterns.
findings.evidence: FlexFolderSystem.cs lines 18-45 list the ExcludePatterns.Add calls including "**.xml", "**.zip", "**.flextext"; Chorus ProjectFolderConfiguration: 'NB: These take precedence over any includePatterns.' AddExcludedVideoExtensions adds "**." + each of mpa, mpe, mpg, mpeg, mpv2, mp2, mp4, mov, wmv, rm, avi, wvx, m1v.
findings.implication: A .json (or .txt) file under LinkedFiles/Others is included. Do NOT use .xml or .zip for the FDAT file — both are globally excluded even inside LinkedFiles. Also avoid **.flextext.

findings.claim: The Mercurial repository root is the FLEx project folder (the directory containing the .fwdata), and include/exclude patterns are resolved relative to it. Consequently LinkedFiles only sync when LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir is the default <project>/LinkedFiles; a project whose Linked Files folder has been relocated (allowed by FLEx, e.g. to a network share) syncs no linked files at all.
findings.evidence: SendReceiveActionHandler: 'var projectDir = Path.GetDirectoryName(options["-p"]); using (var chorusSystem = TriboroughBridgeUtilities.InitializeChorusSystem(projectDir, ..., FlexFolderSystem.ConfigureChorusProjectFolder))'. HgRepository.AddAndCheckinFiles: 'string p = Path.Combine(_pathToRepository, pattern); args.Append(" -I " + ...)'. LCM LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir getter: 'return String.IsNullOrEmpty(LinkedFilesRootDir_Generated) ? Path.Combine(m_cache.ProjectId.ProjectFolder, LcmFileHelper.ksLinkedFilesDir) : LinkedFilesRelativePathHelper.GetLinkedFilesFullPathFromRelativePath(...)'. Model comment: 'It could be a physical path name (e.g., c:\FwData) or a network name that could be accessed by other users (e.g., \\ls-daffy\FwData).'
findings.implication: FDAT must compute the target folder as LcmFileHelper.GetOtherExternalFilesDir(langProject.LinkedFilesRootDir) and warn (or fall back to a model-based store) when LinkedFilesRootDir is not inside cache.ProjectId.ProjectFolder, because then the JSON will silently not be shared.

findings.claim: LCM defines the LinkedFiles folder names as constants: LinkedFiles, AudioVisual, Pictures, Others; helper methods GetDefaultOtherExternalFilesDir(projectPath) = <project>/LinkedFiles/Others and GetOtherExternalFilesDir(linkedFilesRoot) = <root>/Others.
findings.evidence: public const string ksLinkedFilesDir = "LinkedFiles"; ksMediaDir = "AudioVisual"; ksPicturesDir = "Pictures"; ksOtherLinkedFilesDir = "Others"; GetOtherExternalFilesDir(string projectLinkedFilesPath) { return Path.Combine(projectLinkedFilesPath, ksOtherLinkedFilesDir); }
findings.implication: Use these constants (reachable from flexlibs via the SIL.LCModel assembly) rather than hard-coding folder names.

findings.claim: Chorus runs LargeFileFilter before every commit. The maximum size for a file is looked up by extension from the installed file-type handlers; an extension no handler claims (which includes 'json') gets the default of exactly 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes). Images (bmp, jpg, jpeg, gif, png, tif, tiff, ico, wmf, pcx, cgm) and audio (wav, snd, au, aif, aifc, aiff, wma, mp3, webm) get 10 MiB; .txt and .lift are unlimited; FlexBridge's own split-file extensions are unlimited (int.MaxValue). The '10 MB' mentioned in the 2022 comment is implemented only in the image/audio handlers, not in the default.
findings.evidence: LargeFileFilter: 'public static uint Megabyte => 1048576;' ... 'if (!extensionToMaximumSize.TryGetValue(extension, out maxForExtension)) { maxForExtension = Megabyte; }'. Synchronizer.Commit: 'string tooLargeFilesMessage = LargeFileFilter.FilterFiles(Repository, _project, _handlers);'. DefaultFileTypeHandler.MaximumFileSize returns LargeFileFilter.Megabyte and GetExtensionsOfKnownTextFileTypes yields nothing; ImageFileTypeHandler/AudioFileTypeHandler return 'LargeFileFilter.Megabyte * 10'; TextFileTypeHandler ('txt') and LiftFileHandler return UInt32.MaxValue. FlexBridge: 'uint IChorusFileTypeHandler.MaximumFileSize => int.MaxValue;' with GetExtensionsOfKnownTextFileTypes = '_handlers.Select(handlerStrategy => handlerStrategy.Extension)' (its FLEx split-file extensions).
findings.implication: An FDAT .json is hard-capped at 1 MiB per file. Keep one file per chart (or per text), keep it compact (no pretty-printing, no embedded chart data), and have FDAT refuse to write past ~900 KB. Naming the file .txt would remove the cap (and change merge behaviour, see below).

findings.claim: An oversized file is not an error: Chorus appends its path to ExcludePatterns, and if the file is already tracked (status M or A) it runs 'hg forget' on it, so it stops being versioned; the user only gets a warning line in the Send/Receive progress log.
findings.evidence: 'File '{0}' is too large to include in the Send/Receive system. It is {1}, but the maximum allowed is {2}. The file is at {3}.' / 'has grown too large ...'; 'configuration.ExcludePatterns.Add(shortPathname); if (forgetItIfTooLarge) repository.ForgetFile(shortPathname);' with forgetItIfTooLarge = true for status "M" and "A". Synchronizer: 'We're sorry, but the Send/Receive system can't handle large files. The following files won't be stored or shared ...' written via _progress.WriteWarning.
findings.implication: If the FDAT JSON grows past 1 MiB, colleagues silently stop receiving updates (they keep the last small version). FDAT must enforce the limit itself and surface it in its UI.

findings.claim: No handler can merge a .json: FlexBridge's single IChorusFileTypeHandler answers CanMergeFile/CanDiffFile via CanValidateFile, which dispatches on extension to its per-extension strategies and falls to UnknownFileTypeHandlerStrategy (CanValidateFile returns false); Chorus's own handlers claim only .txt, .lift, images, audio, etc. ChorusMerge therefore uses DefaultFileTypeHandler.
findings.evidence: FieldWorksCommonFileHandler: 'bool IChorusFileTypeHandler.CanMergeFile(string pathToFile) { return AsIChorusFileTypeHandler.CanValidateFile(pathToFile); }' ... 'var handler = GetHandlerFromExtension(extension.Substring(1)); return handler.CanValidateFile(pathToFile);' with 'GetHandlerFromExtension ... ?? _unknownFileTypeHandler'; UnknownFileTypeHandlerStrategy.CanValidateFile 'return false;'. Chorus TextFileTypeHandler.CanMergeFile: 'return (Path.GetExtension(pathToFile) == ".txt");'. ChorusFileTypeHandlerCollection.GetHandlerForMerging: 'return handler ?? new DefaultFileTypeHandler();'. ChorusMerge Program: 'var handler = handlers.GetHandlerForMerging(order.pathToOurs); ... handler.Do3WayMerge(order);'.
findings.implication: There is no element-level or line-level merge for the FDAT JSON; conflict resolution is whole-file (next finding).

findings.claim: When both sides changed a .json, DefaultFileTypeHandler.Do3WayMerge records an UnmergableFileTypeConflict in the merge listener (written to a .NewChorusNotes file next to the data) and, because Chorus always runs the merge in 'WeWin' mode, leaves the merging machine's own version in place; the other user's version is only in Mercurial history. In 'TheyWin' mode it would copy theirs over ours; there is no combining.
findings.evidence: DefaultFileTypeHandler.Do3WayMerge: 'XmlMergeService.AddConflictToListener(mergeOrder.EventListener, new UnmergableFileTypeConflict(mergeOrder.MergeSituation)); switch (...ConflictHandlingMode) { default: // just leave our file there ... case WeWin: break; case TheyWin: File.Copy(mergeOrder.pathToTheirs, mergeOrder.pathToOurs, true); }'. Synchronizer: 'Go with WeWin, since that is the default ... using (new ShortTermEnvironmentalVariable(MergeOrder.kConflictHandlingModeEnvVarName, MergeOrder.ConflictHandlingModeChoices.WeWin.ToString()))'; MergeSituation.CreateFromEnvironmentVariables defaults 'var mode = MergeOrder.ConflictHandlingModeChoices.WeWin;'. ChorusMerge Program: 'using (var xmlListener = new ChorusNotesMergeEventListener(order.pathToOurs + ".NewChorusNotes"))'.
findings.implication: Two linguists annotating the same chart between syncs lose one side's work (the side that did not perform the merge). Mitigations: one file per chart (conflicts only when the same chart is edited), or keep frequently-edited data in LCM objects, or have FDAT detect the ChorusNotes conflict record. Same whole-file semantics as the custom-field-string option in PLAN.md §5, but with the extra 1 MiB cap and no FLEx visibility.

findings.claim: Naming the file with a .txt extension changes both constraints: Chorus's TextFileTypeHandler claims .txt with no size limit and merges it line-by-line with diff3 (Windows: bundled diff3.exe), but it throws on an overlapping-line conflict; ChorusMerge then exits with code 1 ('ChorusMerge Error'), and what Mercurial/Chorus does with the file after a failed merge tool is not established here.
findings.evidence: TextFileTypeHandler: CanMergeFile '== ".txt"'; Do3WayMerge calls GetRawMerge via diff3 '-m'; RunProcess: 'if(result.ExitCode == 1) throw new ApplicationException("Could not merge text files without conflict: " ...'; MaximumFileSize 'return UInt32.MaxValue;'; '_diff3Exe = Platform.IsWindows ? "diff3/bin/diff3.exe" : "diff3"'. Program.cs catch: 'ErrorWriter.WriteLine("ChorusMerge Error: " + e.Message); ... return 1;'.
findings.implication: A line-oriented JSON (one record per line, sorted by GUID) saved as .txt would auto-merge non-overlapping edits by different users and lift the 1 MiB cap, but the conflict path is unverified and risky; only consider after a two-machine test. FlexBridge's handler declines .txt too (unknown extension), so Chorus's text handler is the one that runs — inferred from MEF FirstOrDefault over both handler sets.

findings.claim: The synced FDAT file needs no LCM object at all: Send/Receive adds files purely by location/pattern ('hg add -I ... -X ...'), and deletions in the working directory are recorded and propagated ('hg rm -A').
findings.evidence: AddAndCheckinFiles: builds -I/-X arguments from the patterns, 'if (GetIsAtLeastOneMissingFileInWorkingDir()) { ... Execute(..., "rm -A"); }' then 'Execute(..., "add", args)'.
findings.implication: FDAT can write LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/<chartGuid>.json without any LCM write transaction and it will sync; an LCM pointer (CmFile/CmMediaURI) is optional and only matters for FLEx backup and discoverability. FLEx is not notified when the file changes after S/R — FDAT must re-read on demand (inferred: nothing in FLEx watches LinkedFiles/Others).

findings.claim: CmFile.InternalPath is a Unicode path stored relative to LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir (or absolute if rooted); the setter strips the LinkedFilesRootDir prefix, and AbsoluteInternalPath re-combines it. CmFile objects are owned by CmFolder.Files; LangProject owns folder collections Pictures ('Local Pictures'), Media ('Local Media') and one FilePathsInTsStrings folder ('File paths in TsStrings'). CmFile is referenced by CmPicture.PictureFile and CmMedia.MediaFile (CmMedia owned by LexPronunciation.MediaFiles), and owned directly by ScrImportSFFiles.Files.
findings.evidence: Model: '<class ... id="CmFile"> <basic id="OriginalPath" sig="Unicode"/> <basic id="InternalPath" sig="Unicode"/>'; '<class id="CmFolder"> ... <owning id="Files" card="col" sig="CmFile"/>'; LangProject '<owning num="48" id="Pictures" card="col" sig="CmFolder"/>', '<owning num="51" id="Media" card="col" sig="CmFolder"> ... one CmFolder called "Local Media"', '<owning num="56" id="FilePathsInTsStrings" card="atomic" sig="CmFolder"> ... holds all externalLink's to files found in TsStrings'; CmPicture '<rel id="PictureFile" sig="CmFile"/>'; CmMedia '<rel id="MediaFile" sig="CmFile">'. Code: 'Gets or sets the InternalPath (relative to the LinkedFilesRootDir). Alternatively it may be an absolute path'; setter 'LinkedFilesRelativePathHelper.GetRelativeLinkedFilesPath(value, m_cache.LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir)'; constants LocalPictures = "Local Pictures", LocalMedia = "Local Media", LocalFilePathsInTsStrings = "File paths in TsStrings". DomainObjectServices.FindOrCreateFile(folder, srcFile) creates a CmFile in a folder.
findings.implication: If FDAT wants FLEx to 'know' about its file, the cleanest FLEx-native pointer is a CmFile (InternalPath = 'Others/fdat/<guid>.json') in a dedicated CmFolder (e.g. named 'FDAT') added to LangProject.MediaOC via DomainObjectServices.FindOrCreateFolder/FindOrCreateFile — the same mechanism FLEx uses for pronunciation media. FLEx shows nothing for unreferenced CmFiles, so it is invisible and harmless. This is an inference from the mechanism, not something FLEx documents.

findings.claim: FLEx's own 'Insert Link to File' (Insert menu, CmdInsertLinkToFile) and 'Insert media file' commands prompt the user to move/copy/leave the file; links go to LinkedFiles/Others and media to LinkedFiles/AudioVisual. A link becomes a TsString run whose ObjData starts with (char)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName followed by the path/URL, and a CmFile is registered in LangProject.FilePathsInTsStrings; clicking it launches the default application for the file.
findings.evidence: FwXWindow.OnInsertLinkToFile: 'pathname = MoveOrCopyFilesController.MoveCopyOrLeaveExternalFile(pathname, Cache.LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir, ...); helper.ConvertSelToLink(pathname, StyleSheet);'. MoveOrCopyFilesController: MoveCopyOrLeaveExternalFile uses Path.Combine(sRootDirLinkedFiles, LcmFileHelper.ksOtherLinkedFilesDir); MoveCopyOrLeaveMediaFiles uses ksMediaDir; 'if (files.All(f => IsFileInFolder(f, sRootDirExternalLinks))) return files;' otherwise shows MoveOrCopyFilesDlg and File.Move/File.Copy. RootSiteEditingHelper.ConvertSelToLink: 'var filename = StringServices.MarkTextInBldrAsHyperlink(tsb, 0, tsb.Length, clip, hyperlinkStyle, m_cache.LanguageProject.LinkedFilesRootDir); if (FileUtils.IsFilePathValid(filename)) { ... DomainObjectServices.FindOrCreateFile(m_cache.LangProject.FilePathsInTsStringsOA, filename); }'. StringSlice.DoHotLinkAction: 'if (strData[0] == (int)FwObjDataTypes.kodtExternalPathName) { string url = strData.Substring(1); // may also be just a file name, launches default app.' TsStringUtils.GetURL prefixes 'file://' for non-URL paths. Main.xml: '<command id="CmdInsertLinkToFile" label="L_ink to File..." message="InsertLinkToFile" icon="ExternalLink"/>'.
findings.implication: LinkedFiles/Others is precisely FLEx's designated home for 'other' user files, so an fdat/ subfolder there is consistent with FLEx conventions. An external-link run in, e.g., the Text's Comment field could point at the FDAT file, but that is user-visible text and not appropriate for machine data.

findings.claim: CmMediaURI has a single Unicode property MediaURI ('the location and offset of the media file ... subset of the MediaFragment specification'); a Text owns one CmMediaContainer (Text.MediaFiles, atomic) which owns any number of CmMediaURIs (MediaURIs, collection) plus one OffsetType string; Segment.MediaURI references one of them with BeginTimeOffset/EndTimeOffset. LCM has no override for MediaURI: it is stored verbatim, not made relative to LinkedFilesRootDir. So yes, a Text can carry several CmMediaURIs.
findings.evidence: '<class num="72" id="CmMediaURI"> ... Currently a placeholder for ELAN data, not modifiable or viewable in flex as of Nov 2011 ... <basic num="1" id="MediaURI" sig="Unicode">'; '<class num="73" id="CmMediaContainer"> This class collects any number of MediaURIs ... <basic id="OffsetType" sig="Unicode"/> <owning num="2" id="MediaURIs" card="col" sig="CmMediaURI"/>'; Text '<owning num="12" id="MediaFiles" card="atomic" sig="CmMediaContainer">'; Segment '<rel num="7" id="MediaURI" sig="CmMediaURI" card="atomic">'. grep of DomainImpl shows only CmMediaURIFactory.Create(cache, guid) (FactoryAdditions.cs:2734-2745) and no CmMediaURI partial class in OverridesCellar.cs.
findings.implication: Model-wise the owner's idea is legal: FDAT could add a CmMediaURI to Text.MediaFilesOA.MediaURIsOC whose MediaURI is a file: URI to the JSON, without touching any existing media entry. But MediaURI is an absolute URI string in practice (see FLEx behaviour below), which differs per machine unless FDAT re-resolves it; the file syncs regardless of the pointer.

findings.claim: In the current FLEx, a Text's CmMediaURIs are visible read-only: the Text 'Info' tab (layout Text/FullInformation) has a 'Media' field rendered by MediaInfoSlice, which lists every MediaURI as a non-editable paragraph (showing Uri.LocalPath if the string parses as a URI, else the raw string). FLEx offers no UI to add or edit them; the only creation path is FLExText (BIRD) import, which sets MediaURI = the <media location> attribute with no validation, and the interlinear XML export writes them back out as <media-files offset-type><media guid location>.
findings.evidence: Cellar.fwlayout: '<layout class="Text" type="detail" name="FullInformation"> ... <part ref="Media"/>'; CellarParts.xml: '<part id="Text-Detail-Media"> <slice label="Media" field="MediaFiles" editor="custom" ... class="...MediaInfoSlice"'. MediaInfoSlice: 'A slice that displays the media file URIs as static text'; MediaInfoVc.Display: '// Make non-editable ... foreach (var medUri in m_mediaURIs) { string uriString = medUri.MediaURI; try { Uri uri = new Uri(uriString); uriString = uri.LocalPath; } catch { } ... vwenv.AddString(tss); }'. Only writers in the checkout: BIRDInterlinearImporter 'newText.MediaFilesOA.MediaURIsOC.Add(media); ... media.MediaURI = mediaFile.location;'. Exporter: 'm_writer.WriteStartElement("media-files"); ... WriteAttributeString("location", mediaFile.MediaURI);'.
findings.implication: If FDAT registered its JSON as a CmMediaURI, the linguist would see an extra line like 'C:\...\LinkedFiles\Others\fdat\<guid>.json' under Media in the text's Info tab, could not remove it in FLEx, and it would travel through FLExText export/import as if it were a recording. A .json URI is never validated or opened by FLEx. Not harmful, but it misuses an ELAN-media slot; prefer no pointer or a CmFile in a dedicated folder.

findings.claim: FLEx only tries to open a CmMediaURI when a Segment references it: InterlinVc shows a 'No Media' message unless the URI parses, has the file: scheme and the file exists; InterlinDocForAnalysis.StartMediaPlay does 'new Uri(mediaUri)' and plays only 'if (uri.IsFile && File.Exists(uri.LocalPath))' via NAudio. A relative path would fail Uri parsing (UriFormatException) — the display code catches it, the playback code does not.
findings.evidence: InterlinVc.CheckFileExistsFromUri: 'Uri uri = new Uri(uriString); if (uri.IsFile) { ... return File.Exists(localPath); } else { ... return false; }' catch (UriFormatException) return false; caller: 'if (!fileExists) { ... AddNoMediaMessage(...); return; }'. InterlinDocForAnalysis: 'var mediaUri = segment.MediaURIRA?.MediaURI; Uri uri = new Uri(mediaUri); if (uri.IsFile && File.Exists(uri.LocalPath)) { m_outputDevice = new WaveOutEvent(); ... m_audioFile = new AudioFileReader(uri.LocalPath);'
findings.implication: As long as FDAT never sets Segment.MediaURIRA to its entry, FLEx will never attempt to play the JSON. If it did, AudioFileReader would fail on a .json (inferred). MediaURI values are absolute URIs in practice, so a synced pointer would show a colleague the original author's path.

findings.claim: FLEx's project backup includes every file under LinkedFiles when the folder is inside the project folder and 'include linked files' is selected; if LinkedFiles is elsewhere, only files with a CmFile object in LangProject.Media/Pictures/FilePathsInTsStrings folders are backed up.
findings.evidence: 'if (m_settings.IncludeLinkedFiles) foreach (string file in GetAudioVisualAndPicturesAndOtherFiles()) yield return file;' ... 'If the LinkedFiles folder is located inside the project folder, return all the files under this folder. If the LinkedFiles folder is located in some other location, then only return the file paths for which there is a CmFile object in the database.' GetLinkedFilesFromCmFiles walks lp.MediaOC, lp.PicturesOC and lp.FilePathsInTsStringsOA.
findings.implication: A JSON under an in-project LinkedFiles/Others is covered by FLEx Backup/Restore (when the user ticks linked files); registering a CmFile extends that to relocated LinkedFiles folders. CmMediaURI entries are NOT consulted by backup.

findings.claim: FieldWorks/Chorus rationale for the size cap: a single large committed file makes the repository unusable for the whole team, so the limit is enforced per commit; Chorus does not detect binary vs text — it decides purely by extension.
findings.evidence: LargeFileFilter header: 'if even one large file is committed to the repo, that repo is completely dead for all users of that project'; 'The 1MB limit set in 2011 was revisited ... increasing the limit to 10 MB. This will allow the inclusion of high-quality photos and .wav files up to 56 seconds' (implemented in image/audio handlers only). GetStatusOfFilesOfInterest keys files by 'Path.GetExtension(filename)' lowercased.
findings.implication: Do not rely on the cap ever being raised for .json; design for small per-chart files.

findings.claim: flexlibs exposes nothing specific to linked files or media; FDAT would call LCM directly (LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir, LcmFileHelper) through the pythonnet-loaded SIL.LCModel assembly.
findings.evidence: grep -i 'linkedfiles|MediaFiles|CmFile|CmMediaURI' over flexlibs/flexlibs/code/FLExProject.py and flexlibs/docs returns no hits (only LcmFileLockedException).
findings.implication: The sidecar needs a small LCM-level helper for the linked-files path; no flexlibs feature to lean on.

openQuestions: Two-machine confirmation (PLAN.md Phase 0) that a file created under LinkedFiles/Others/fdat/ by an external process is picked up by the next Send/Receive without FLEx having any object referencing it; the include pattern says yes, but hg's handling of '**.*' for nested subfolders should be verified on a real repo.

What Chorus/Mercurial does with a .txt file when TextFileTypeHandler's diff3 merge throws on an overlapping conflict (ChorusMerge returns exit code 1) — needed before considering a line-mergeable .txt format instead of an opaque .json.

Whether the UnmergableFileTypeConflict note for a .json in LinkedFiles/Others is surfaced anywhere the user will see it (FLExBridge's conflict report/notes browser) — the note is written to <file>.NewChorusNotes and later renamed to .ChorusNotes by Chorus, but presentation of non-FLEx files was not traced.
Whether the installed FieldWorks version still ships MediaInfoSlice (the file's copyright is 2026, i.e. very recent); older FLEx versions show nothing for Text.MediaFiles at all.
If the FDAT JSON needs a per-machine absolute path (as a CmMediaURI would), how it should be re-resolved on each machine; a CmFile.InternalPath is relative and avoids the issue.
Behaviour when LangProject.LinkedFilesRootDir points outside the project folder (shared drive): FDAT must decide between writing there (shared by filesystem, not by S/R) and refusing/warning.

sweep:discourse-code.summary:
INVESTIGATION "discourse-code" (FieldWorks Src/LexText/Discourse + LCM discourse model). All paths are relative to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fdat/fb1d7f18-f46f-5695-b961-37c4221bc0d5/scratchpad/src unless absolute.

(A) EXACT 'Export Text Chart' XML (the "Discourse XML" item = Plain.xml, mode="doNothing", i.e. the raw DiscourseExporter output; the Word/XLingPaper items run an XSLT over it). The exporter is an IVwEnv that intercepts the same view-constructor calls that draw the on-screen chart (ConstChartVc.kfragPrintChart), so the XML mirrors the display, including bracket/space literals from ConstituentChartStyleInfo.xml. Written with XmlTextWriter, UTF-8, text NFC-normalised, in this order:

<document>
  <chart>
    <!-- one title row per header level, N = depth of the template tree (MultilevelHeaderModel) -->
    <row type="title1">                                   (type="title{n}", n counts from 1 in output order)
      <cell cols="1"><main /></cell>                       (row-number header: ALWAYS empty)
      <cell cols="K"><main><lit lang="en">Group name</lit></main></cell> ...   (K = number of leaf columns under the node; a leaf directly under the template root is labelled here and gets an empty placeholder cell in every lower title row)
      <cell cols="1"><main><lit lang="analWs">Notes</lit></main></cell>       (Notes header ONLY in the first title row; in lower rows an empty cell; placed FIRST in the row when NotesColumnOnRight=false; whole row reversed for RTL charts)
    </row>
    <row type="title2"> ... leaf column names as <lit lang=..> ... </row>
    <!-- data rows -->
    <row [endPara="true" | endSent="true"] type="normal|dependent|speech|song" [id="1a"]>   (attribute order: endPara/endSent, type, id; only ONE of endPara/endSent is written, endPara wins; id = ConstChartRow.Label text, omitted when empty)
      [<cell cols="1"><main><note lang="..">...</note></main></cell>]   (notes cell here when notes column is on the left)
      <cell cols="1"><main><rownum lang="en">1a</rownum></main></cell>  (Label ws is always English)
      <cell [reversed="true"] cols="N"><main>...</main>[<glosses><gloss lang="analWs">..</gloss>...</glosses>]</cell> ... one <cell> per template column, merged cells span N columns, empty columns are <cell cols="1"><main /></cell> (or <main><lit lang="analWs">---</lit></main> in columns whose English name is "Subject" or "Verb": automatic missing marker)
      [<cell cols="1"><main><note lang="..">...</note></main></cell>]   (notes cell here when NotesColumnOnRight, the default; an empty Notes still produces an empty <note lang=".."/> element)
    </row>
  </chart>
  <languages>                                              (AFTER chart, only writing systems actually used)
    <language lang="xyz" font="Charis SIL" [vernacular="true"] [RightToLeft="true"]/>
  </languages>
</document>

Contents of <main> in order of the row's CellsOS (parts in the same cell are separated by a space string that the exporter drops):
 - ConstChartWordGroup: for each WORDFORM occurrence from BeginSegment/BeginAnalysisIndex to EndSegment/EndAnalysisIndex (punctuation occurrences skipped) → <word [moved="true"] lang="vernWs">baseline text</word> (attribute order moved, lang; moved="true" when a ConstChartMovedTextMarker points at this group); its gloss (WfiGloss.Form in the analysis ws, or literally *** when the analysis has no gloss) is buffered and emitted after </main> inside <glosses>. Only the Word and Word Gloss lines are exported (default chart line choices).
 - ConstChartTag with TagRA: <lit noSpaceAfter="true" lang="analWs">(</lit><listRef lang="ws">ABBR</listRef><lit noSpaceBefore="true" lang="analWs">)</lit>; text = CmPossibility.Abbreviation in the first analysis ws that has one, else Name. If it is the first part of a Subject/Verb cell, <lit>---</lit> is inserted before it.
 - ConstChartTag with TagRA=null (user missing marker): <lit lang="analWs">---</lit>.
 - ConstChartClauseMarker: <lit noSpaceAfter="true" lang="analWs">[</lit><clauseMkr target="1b" lang="en">1b</clauseMkr>[<lit noSpaceAfter="true" lang="analWs">-</lit><clauseMkr target="1c" lang="en">1c</clauseMkr>]<lit noSpaceBefore="true" lang="analWs">]</lit> (first and last dependent row label only; brackets from dependentMkr/speechMkr/songMkr style entries = "[]").
 - ConstChartMovedTextMarker: <moveMkr lang="userWs" [targetFirstOnLine="false"]>Preposed</moveMkr> or ...>Postposed</moveMkr> (NOT << / >>; those are on-screen only; targetFirstOnLine="false" when an earlier moved word group exists in the target's row).
 - Dependent/speech/song rows: <lit noSpaceAfter="true" lang="analWs">[</lit> before the first word group of a StartDependentClauseGroup row and <lit noSpaceBefore="true" lang="analWs">]</lit> after the last word group of an EndDependentClauseGroup row (list-ref tags stay outside the brackets; an auto-missing Subject/Verb column shifts the bracket into that cell).
 - lit spacing rule: noSpaceBefore if the literal starts with ] or ); noSpaceAfter if it ends with [ ( or -.
 Merged cells: MergesBefore → one cell covering every unoccupied column up to and including the part's column (reversed="true" when it spans >1); MergesAfter → cols = distance to the next part's column (one less if that next part MergesBefore and there are ≥2 empty columns), or all remaining columns.

DISCREPANCIES vs /home/user/fdat/test/fixtures/sample-chart.xml (synthetic) and desktop/sidecar/fdat_lcm.py (which mirrors the fixture): languages emitted before chart (FLEx: after); no lang attributes anywhere (FLEx: on every word/gloss/lit/listRef/clauseMkr/rownum/note); title cells hold bare text and "#"/"Row"/"Notes" labels in both header rows (FLEx: <main><lit lang>, empty row-number header, Notes header only in title1, no cols omitted); data cells omit cols (FLEx always writes cols); rows lack id (FLEx: id=label) and put type before endSent (FLEx: endSent/endPara first) and the sidecar writes both endSent and endPara (FLEx: one); listRef without the "(" ")" lits; clauseMkr without target and without "[" "]" lits and with a single "1b-1c" text (FLEx: two clauseMkr + "-" lit); dependent/speech rows without "[" "]" lits; the speech row's quote lits never occur in FLEx output; empty Notes cell as <main/> (FLEx: empty <note lang>); moved text as <lit><<</lit> (FLEx: <moveMkr>Preposed/Postposed + moved="true" on the words); missing markers (---) absent. PLAN §4 table: the ConstChartMovedTextMarker row ("<lit> with << / >>") and the ConstChartClauseMarker row ("1b-1c") are wrong; the template row assumes exactly two title levels (FLEx emits one per tree depth with placeholders); Label also feeds the row id attribute; the Notes cell position is a per-user setting, not data; languages carry font/vernacular/RightToLeft. The renderer's XSLT (docs/textchart/textchart-to-html.xsl) only treats title1/title2 as header rows and only uses `cell[1]` for the row label, so notes-on-left charts and 3-level templates would mis-render.

(B) MODEL/EDITING BEHAVIOUR: a ConstChartRow is a clause with Notes (single formatted String, not multilingual), ClauseType (Integer enum Normal=0, Dependent=1, Song=2, Speech=3), EndParagraph, EndSentence, Start/EndDependentClauseGroup, Cells (owning seq) and Label (String, English ws, recomputed by RenumberRows on any insert/delete/end-of-sentence change, so labels are NOT stable keys). Rows do not reference segments; only ConstChartWordGroup does (BeginSegment/EndSegment + analysis indices); the chart's text is DsConstChart.BasedOnRA. GUID stability: moving a cell into an EMPTY cell/row keeps the word-group object (ColumnRA change or CellsOS.MoveTo, which re-inserts the same object); merging into an OCCUPIED cell grows the destination word group and deletes the source; moving single words shrinks/grows existing groups and deletes emptied ones or creates new ones; InsertRow creates a new row; 'Clear chart from here' deletes rows and parts outright; a row deletes itself automatically when its last cell part is removed unless it has non-empty Notes, and RemoveMissingMarker recreates such a row with a NEW GUID; chart open runs CleanupInvalidChartCells which deletes invalid parts and, if no word groups remain, clears all rows (dumping Notes to <project>/SavedNotes.txt). Notes are edited in place in the chart view (the only editable cell). ConstChartTag.TagRA is not validated against DsDiscourseData.ChartMarkersOA anywhere: the menu is built from that list, but display/factory accept any CmPossibility. Template: DsChart.TemplateRA = a top-level possibility of DsDiscourseData.ConstChartTempl; leaves (depth-first) are the columns referenced by ColumnRA, non-leaves are column groups (any depth); auto-missing markers are hard-wired to English column names "Subject"/"Verb"; one chart per (text, template) pair; the last-used chart, notes-on-right, column widths and line choices live in the user's PropertyTable, not the model. All colours/brackets/underlines come from the installed ConstituentChartStyleInfo.xml (per clause type / part kind); no per-row, per-cell or per-marker style or user-data hook exists in the chart code, and CmPossibility.ForeColor/BackColor/Hidden are never read by it. DsChart inherits CmMajorObject.Name/Description/DateCreated/DateModified, which the chart UI never touches (possible chart-level home, unverified elsewhere).

findings.claim: The 'Discourse XML' export item writes the raw DiscourseExporter output with no transform; only the Word and XLingPaper items post-process it with an XSLT.
findings.evidence: Plain.xml: FxtDocumentDescription dataLabel="Discourse XML" ... mode="doNothing"; MsWord.xml mode="applySingleTransform" transform="Discourse2Word.xsl"; DoExport: case "doNothing": break; case "applySingleTransform": exporter.PostProcess(sTransform, outPath, 1); ExportPhase1 creates new XmlTextWriter(fileName, UTF8) and calls exporter.ExportDisplay().
findings.implication: The sidecar must reproduce DiscourseExporter's element shape exactly; there is no hidden transform to account for.

findings.claim: Document skeleton: <document><chart>...</chart><languages>...</languages></document> — the languages block comes AFTER the chart, and lists only writing systems actually used, each as <language lang= font= [vernacular="true"] [RightToLeft="true"]/>.
findings.evidence: ExportDisplay: WriteStartElement("document"); WriteStartElement("chart"); m_vc.Display(this, OpenObject, ConstChartVc.kfragPrintChart); WriteEndElement(); WriteLanguages(); WriteEndElement(). WriteLanguages loops m_usedWritingSystems writing attributes lang=ws.Id, font=ws.DefaultFontName, vernacular="true" if in VernacularWritingSystems, RightToLeft="true" if ws.RightToLeftScript.
findings.implication: Fixture and sidecar put <languages> first and omit vernacular/RightToLeft; harmless for the tolerant renderer but not byte-equivalent.

findings.claim: Title rows: one <row type="title{n}"> per header level (n from 1, top level first); each header cell is <cell cols="K"><main><lit lang="..">Label</lit></main></cell>; the row-number header cell is always empty <cell cols="1"><main /></cell>; the Notes header <lit>Notes</lit> appears only in the first title row (empty cell in the others); Notes header is placed first when NotesColumnOnRight is false; RTL charts reverse the cell order.
findings.evidence: OpenTableRow: default branch writes type=$"title{++m_titleRowCount}". PrintAnyLevelColumnHeaders(depth): if (!(NotesColumnOnRight ^ IsRightToLeft)) PrintNotesCellHeader(..., depth == 0); PrintRowNumCellHeader; foreach header: OpenStandardCell(rtlDecorator, header.ColumnCount, header.IsLastInGroup); if (header.Label != null) rtlDecorator.AddString(header.Label); ... rtlDecorator.FlushDecorator() // if RTL, put out headers reversed. AddString of non-word text writes <lit> with lang. Tests: VerifyColumnGroupTitleRow expects cell cols=2 'prenuclear', cols=3 'nucleus', cols=1 'postnuc', Notes only when titleRowCount==2; VerifyColumnTitleRow expects the postnuc position to be a placeholder cell when a group row exists.
findings.implication: The fixture/sidecar emit '#','Row','Notes' text cells without <main>/<lit> and label Notes in both rows; PLAN §4 assumes exactly two title levels, but FLEx emits one per template depth with placeholder cells. FDAT's XSLT only recognises title1/title2.

findings.claim: Data row element: <row [endPara="true"|endSent="true"] type="normal|dependent|speech|song" [id="label"]>; attribute order is endPara/endSent, then type, then id; only one of endPara/endSent is written (endPara takes precedence); id is omitted when Label is empty.
findings.evidence: OpenTableRow case kfragChartRow: if (row.EndParagraph) WriteAttributeString("endPara","true"); else if (row.EndSentence) WriteAttributeString("endSent","true"); var clauseType = ConstChartVc.GetRowStyleName(row); WriteAttributeString("type", clauseType); var label = row.Label.Text; if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(label)) WriteAttributeString("id", label). GetRowStyleName maps ClauseTypes.Dependent→"dependent", Speech→"speech", Song→"song", default "normal".
findings.implication: Sidecar writes both endSent and endPara and omits id; fixture omits id. Add id=label and follow the else-if rule.

findings.claim: Data row cell order is: [notes cell if notes on left], row-number cell <cell cols="1"><main><rownum lang="en">1a</rownum></main></cell>, one cell per template column, [notes cell if notes on right]. The Label writing system is always English.
findings.evidence: MakeCellsMethod.Run: if (!(NotesColumnOnRight ^ fRtL)) MakeNoteCell(); MakeRowLabelCell(); MakeMainCellParts(); if (NotesColumnOnRight ^ fRtL) MakeNoteCell(). MakeRowLabelCell → OpenRowNumberCell (OpenTableCell(1,1)) + AddStringProp(kflidLabel) → exporter writes "rownum". WsLineNumber returns WritingSystemManager.GetWsFromStr("en"). Test: AssertCellMainChild(row, iCols[0], 1, null, 1, "rownum", "1b", "en").
findings.implication: NotesColumnOnRight is a per-user PropertyTable setting ('notesOnRight'), so the Notes cell can be first or last in a real export; FDAT's XSLT assumes cell[1] is the row label.

findings.claim: Notes cell: <cell cols="1"><main><note lang="..">text</note></main></cell>; an empty/null Notes still yields an empty <note lang=".."/> because the data access returns an empty TsString for a null String property.
findings.evidence: AddStringProp case ConstChartRowTags.kflidNotes: WriteStringProp(tag, "note", 0) → tss = m_sda.get_StringProp(...); WriteStringVal always WriteStartElement/WriteLangAndContent/WriteEndElement. DomainDataByFlid.get_StringProp: if (result != null) return result; ... return TsStringUtils.EmptyString(ws). (INFERRED for the empty case; the export test only checks a row with notes.)
findings.implication: Fixture/sidecar emit <main/> for empty notes; FLEx emits an empty <note>. Renderer tolerant either way.

findings.claim: Cell element: <cell [reversed="true"] cols="N"><main>...</main>[<glosses>...</glosses>]</cell>; reversed is written before cols and only when a MergesBefore cell spans more than one column; glosses are buffered per cell and emitted after </main>.
findings.evidence: OpenTableCell: WriteStartElement("cell"); if (m_fNextCellReversed) { m_fNextCellReversed=false; WriteAttributeString("reversed","true"); } WriteAttributeString("cols", nColSpan); WriteStartElement("main"). set_IntProperty sets m_fNextCellReversed when ktptAlign==ktalTrailing. MakeCellsMethod: if (cellPart.MergesBefore) { if (cColsAvailableUpToCurrent > 1) set_IntProperty(ktptAlign, ktalTrailing); MakeDataCell(cColsAvailableUpToCurrent); }. CloseTableCell writes <glosses><gloss lang=..>..</gloss></glosses> then </cell>.
findings.implication: cols is always present (fixture/sidecar omit it on data cells); reversed must be emitted for MergesBefore spans.

findings.claim: Merged-cell width rule: MergesBefore → one cell covering all unoccupied columns up to and including the part's column; MergesAfter → cols = index of the next part's column minus this column (one less if that next part MergesBefore and there are at least two empty columns), or all remaining columns if none; empty columns are emitted individually as <cell cols="1"><main /></cell>.
findings.evidence: ProcessCurrentCellPart: cColsAvailableUpToCurrent = iHvoNewCol - m_iLastColForWhichCellExists; MergesBefore branch MakeDataCell(cColsAvailableUpToCurrent); else MakeEmptyCells(cColsAvailableUpToCurrent - 1); if (cellPart.MergesAfter) { iNextColumn = AllColumns.Length; loop finds next part in a different column; if (iNextColumn > iHvoNewCol + 2 && nextColCellPart.MergesBefore) iNextColumn--; cColsNext = iNextColumn - iHvoNewCol; } MakeDataCell(cColsNext). MakeEmptyCells opens one cell per column.
findings.implication: PLAN §4 'MergesAfter/MergesBefore → cols spans' is right but the width computation must follow this algorithm (and the sidecar currently ignores merges entirely).

findings.claim: Word groups export one <word [moved="true"] lang="vernWs">baseline text</word> per WORDFORM occurrence in the group (punctuation occurrences are skipped) and one <gloss lang="analWs"> per word after </main>; a word whose analysis has no gloss yields the literal *** gloss. Only the Word and Word-gloss lines are exported by default.
findings.evidence: DisplayWordforms: foreach (var point in wordGrp.GetOccurrences()) DisplayAnalysisAndCloseInnerPile. GetOccurrences: if (curOccurrence.HasWordform) result.Add(...) // word as opposed to punctuation. DisplayWord: IsDoingRealWordForm=true; if (ws == BaselineWs) AddString(baseLineForm) else AddObj(... kfragLineChoices). Exporter AddString: if IsDoingRealWordForm → WriteWordForm("word", tss, ws, m_frags.Contains(kfragMovedTextCellPart) ? "moved" : null); AddStringAltMember case WfiGlossTags.kflidForm → m_glossesInCellCollector.Add; text "***" → collector. GetLineChoices default: kflidWord, kflidWordGloss. Test expects <word moved="true" lang="fr">It</word> and <gloss lang="en">***</gloss>.
findings.implication: The sidecar must iterate wordform occurrences only (skip PunctuationForm analyses), use the segment baseline text (not WfiWordform.Form) and emit moved="true" for moved groups; other interlinear lines a user has enabled are ignored by the exporter (unknown flids hit a Debug.Assert).

findings.claim: ConstChartTag (list marker) exports as <lit noSpaceAfter="true" lang="analWs">(</lit><listRef lang="ws">ABBR</listRef><lit noSpaceBefore="true" lang="analWs">)</lit>; the text is the Abbreviation in the first analysis writing system that has one, falling back to Name; the parentheses come from the 'marker' entry of ConstituentChartStyleInfo.xml.
findings.evidence: kfragChartListItem: ApplyFormatting("marker"); InsertOpenBracket(vwenv,"marker"); AddObjProp(ConstChartTagTags.kflidTag, this, kfragPossibility); InsertCloseBracket. kfragPossibility: flid = kflidAbbreviation; retWs = ActualWs(kwsFirstAnal...); if (retWs == 0) { flid = kflidName; ... } AddStringAltMember(flid, retWs). Exporter: case CmPossibilityTags.kflidName/kflidAbbreviation: WriteStringProp(tag,"listRef",ws). Style file: <marker color="Orange" brackets="()"/>. Test: lit '(' noSpaceAfter, listRef lang=en 'I2', lit ')' noSpaceBefore.
findings.implication: PLAN §7 'chart markers with punctuation' is confirmed: real exports wrap every listRef in ( ) lits; the sidecar should emit them (renderer already strips adhered punctuation) or the web renderer's listRef handling will differ from real exports.

findings.claim: Missing markers export as <lit lang="analWs">---</lit>: automatically in every empty cell (or before the first list marker) of a column whose English name is 'Subject' or 'Verb', and for a user-entered ConstChartTag with TagRA == null.
findings.evidence: ColumnHasAutoMissingMarkers: engLabel == "Subject" || engLabel == "Verb". MakeEmptyCells: if ColumnHasAutoMissingMarkers(iCol) InsertAutoMissingMarker → AddString(m_missMkr); AddCellPartToCell: IsMissingMkr(cellPart) → AddString(m_missMkr); m_missMkr = DiscourseStrings.ksMissingMarker ("---") in DefaultAnalWs. IsListRef requires TagRA != null.
findings.implication: Neither the fixture nor the sidecar emits ---; a real export of the default template always contains them in empty Subject/Verb cells.

findings.claim: Dependent/speech/song rows are bracketed: a <lit noSpaceAfter="true">[</lit> precedes the first word group of a StartDependentClauseGroup row and a <lit noSpaceBefore="true">]</lit> follows the last word group of an EndDependentClauseGroup row; list-marker parts stay outside the brackets; an auto-missing Subject/Verb column after the last part moves the close bracket into that cell.
findings.evidence: MakeMainCellParts: if (m_row.StartDependentClauseGroup) FindCellPartToStartDependentClause(); if (m_row.EndDependentClauseGroup) FindCellPartToEndDependentClause(); GoesInsideClauseBrackets: word group → true; clause placeholder → false; return !IsListRef. FindCellPartToEndDependentClause: if a later auto-missing column exists, m_iCellPartCloseClause = -1 (terminate after auto-marker). Brackets key = GetRowStyleName(row) → style entries speech/song/dependent brackets="[]". Test row type=song: lit '[' then words in a reversed cols=2 cell; ']' after moveMkr in the next cell.
findings.implication: Fixture's 'dependent' and 'speech' rows lack brackets and the speech row uses quote lits that FLEx never generates.

findings.claim: ConstChartClauseMarker exports as <lit noSpaceAfter="true">[</lit><clauseMkr target="1b" lang="en">1b</clauseMkr>[<lit noSpaceAfter="true" lang>-</lit><clauseMkr target="1c" lang="en">1c</clauseMkr>]<lit noSpaceBefore="true">]</lit> — first and last dependent-row labels only, as separate clauseMkr elements, with a target attribute equal to the label.
findings.evidence: DisplayClausePlaceholder: clauseType = GetRowStyleName(hvoClause) + "Mkr"; InsertOpenBracket; AddObjVec(kflidDepClauses, this, kfragClauseLabels); InsertCloseBracket. DisplayVec kfragClauseLabels: AddObj(hvoFirst, kfragComment); if (vecSize==1) break; AddString("-"); AddObj(hvoLast, kfragComment). Exporter AddStringProp kflidLabel with TopFragment==kfragComment: WriteStringProp(tag,"clauseMkr",0,"target", label text). MarkNeedsSpace: EndsWith("-") → noSpaceAfter. Style: dependentMkr/speechMkr/songMkr brackets="[]". Test: lit '[', clauseMkr target=1b lang=en '1b', lit ']'.
findings.implication: PLAN §4 ('Text = 1b, 1b-1c') and the sidecar's single '1b-1c' clauseMkr are wrong; the target attribute is what FLEx's own Word XSLT uses to style the marker.

findings.claim: ConstChartMovedTextMarker exports as <moveMkr lang="userWs" [targetFirstOnLine="false"]>Preposed</moveMkr> or >Postposed</moveMkr> (the on-screen << / >> are replaced), with no brackets; the words of the target word group carry moved="true".
findings.evidence: WriteMTMarker: newTss = tss.Equals(m_sMovedTextBefore) ? "Preposed" : "Postposed"; hvoTarget = get_ObjectProp(kflidWordGroup); if HasPreviousMovedItemOnLine(m_chart,hvoTarget) WriteStringVal("moveMkr", ws, newTss, "targetFirstOnLine", "false") else WriteStringVal("moveMkr",...). kfragMTMarker: AddString(mtt.Preposed ? m_sMovedTextBefore : m_sMovedTextAfter) (ksMovedTextBefore = <<, After = >>). Style entries movedText/movedTextMkr have color only, no brackets. kfragMovedTextCellPart pushes the frag so AddString/AddStringAltMember write moved="true". Discourse2Word.xsl matches moveMkr and @targetFirstOnLine.
findings.implication: PLAN §4's mapping (<lit> with << / >>) and the sidecar's implementation are wrong; FDAT's XSLT already has a moveMkr template, so emitting the real element is the fix.

findings.claim: Literal spacing attributes: noSpaceBefore="true" when the literal starts with ']' or ')', noSpaceAfter="true" when it ends with '[', '(' or '-'; attributes precede lang; directionality marks, empty strings and single spaces are dropped; all text is Unicode-normalised.
findings.evidence: MarkNeedsSpace: if (lit.StartsWith("]") || lit.StartsWith(")")) noSpaceBefore; if (lit.EndsWith("[") || lit.EndsWith("(") || lit.EndsWith("-")) noSpaceAfter. AddString: if (text == "\x200F" || text == "\x200E" || IsNullOrEmpty || text == " ") return; GetText: result.Normalize().
findings.implication: Sidecar should apply the same rule when it emits bracket/dash lits.

findings.claim: ConstChartRow properties: Notes (String — a single formatted TsString, not multilingual), ClauseType (Integer enum Normal=0, Dependent=1, Song=2, Speech=3), EndParagraph, EndSentence, StartDependentClauseGroup, EndDependentClauseGroup (Booleans), Cells (owning seq of ConstituentChartCellPart), Label (String).
findings.evidence: <class num="3" id="ConstChartRow"> <basic num="1" id="Notes" sig="String"/> <basic num="2" id="ClauseType" sig="Integer"> (enum Normal, Dependent, Song, Speech) ... <owning num="7" id="Cells" sig="ConstituentChartCellPart" card="seq"/> <basic num="8" id="Label" sig="String"/>. public enum ClauseTypes { Normal = 0, Dependent = 1, Song = 2, Speech = 3 }.

sweep:tags-and-lists.summary: Text tags (TextTag) and possibility lists are viable, Send/Receive-safe anchors for FDAT, with concrete constraints. TextTag is a small class owned by StText.Tags that references BeginSegment/EndSegment (Segment objects) plus integer analysis indices and one CmPossibility Tag; LCM's TextTagFactory.CreateOnText and the FLEx tagging UI both create them, tags of different tag types may overlap freely (same-type overlaps are replaced), and tags may span segment boundaries (tests exercise 2-segment tags, but code comments and a NotImplementedException show 3+-segment spans are only partially supported). FLEx displays a tag as the possibility's Abbreviation in brackets on its own row under the word bundles - one row per top-level "tag type" - with no colour. The tag list is LangProject.TextMarkupTags, a strict two-level structure (tag types -> tags) enforced by the Lists-area tree handler; FLEx refuses to delete any tag possibility that a TextTag references, or any IsProtected possibility, so a 'Salience' tag type with band sub-tags fits FLEx's own model exactly and is protected by FLEx's own rules. CmPossibility carries ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor/UnderStyle/Hidden integer fields (BGR-encoded, legacy 'overlay' feature) that no FLEx UI in the examined code renders and that the Lists editor explicitly hides, so FDAT can store colours there invisibly and they round-trip through FLExBridge with the list. Custom lists are unowned CmPossibilityLists whose items are CmCustomItem (created via ICmPossibilityListFactory.CreateUnowned, identified by Owner==null, must have a project-unique Name); FLExBridge writes each one to General/UserDefinedLists/UserList-<guid>.list, the TextMarkupTags list to Linguistics/TextCorpus/TextMarkupTags.list, and chart markers to Linguistics/Discourse, all covered by the '**.list' include pattern and 3-way merged. Chart markers (ConstChartTag.Tag) are possibilities in DsDiscourseData.ChartMarkers displayed by Abbreviation, giving stable GUID anchors for FDAT marker styling. Caveats: TextTag anchors to segment+word, not to ConstChartRow, so row salience stored as a TextTag duplicates the row's extent; LCM's AnalysisAdjuster deletes tags whose words are edited away; FLEx's Add Custom Field dialog does not offer CmPossibility/CmCustomItem/ConstChartRow as hosts (only LexEntry, LexSense, LexExampleSentence, MoForm, Segment, RnGenericRec); flexlibs offers only a read helper (UnpackNestedPossibilityList), so FDAT would call LCM factories directly.

findings.claim: TextTag is a CmObject with exactly five properties: BeginSegment and EndSegment (atomic references to Segment), BeginAnalysisIndex and EndAnalysisIndex (integers indexing Segment.Analyses), and Tag (atomic reference to CmPossibility); it is owned in StText.Tags (owning collection).
findings.evidence: <class num="22" id="TextTag" ... base="CmObject"> with <rel num="1" id="BeginSegment" sig="Segment" card="atomic"/>, <rel num="2" id="EndSegment" .../>, <basic num="3" id="BeginAnalysisIndex" sig="Integer"> 'These indices refer to the index of an IAnalysis object in a Segment.Analyses sequence', <basic num="4" id="EndAnalysisIndex" .../>, <rel num="5" id="Tag" sig="CmPossibility" card="atomic"/>. StText: <owning num="3" id="Tags" sig="TextTag" card="col"/>
findings.implication: A TextTag can carry exactly one possibility reference and a word-range; FDAT has no free-text slot on the tag itself. The span is addressed by Segment GUID + integer index (not by analysis GUID), the same addressing ConstChartWordGroup uses, so a chart row's extent and a salience tag can be expressed identically.

findings.claim: LCM provides ITextTagFactory.CreateOnText(begPoint, endPoint, tagPoss) that adds the tag to the owning StText.TagsOC and sets all five properties; it validates only that the points are valid occurrences and tagPoss is non-null - it does NOT check that tagPoss belongs to LangProject.TextMarkupTags.
findings.evidence: public ITextTag CreateOnText(AnalysisOccurrence begPoint, AnalysisOccurrence endPoint, ICmPossibility tagPoss) { if (tagPoss == null) throw ...; if (begPoint == null || !begPoint.IsValid) throw ...; var txt = (IStText)begPoint.Segment.Paragraph.Owner; var newby = Create(); txt.TagsOC.Add(newby); newby.BeginSegmentRA = begPoint.Segment; newby.BeginAnalysisIndex = begPoint.Index; newby.EndSegmentRA = endPoint.Segment; newby.EndAnalysisIndex = endPoint.Index; newby.TagRA = tagPoss; return newby; }
findings.implication: FDAT (via flexlibs/pythonnet) can create tags with one LCM call inside a UndoableUnitOfWork. Because there is no list check, FDAT must itself place Salience possibilities in TextMarkupTags; otherwise the tagging view will not list them and the delete-protection in finding on CanDelete will not apply.

findings.claim: The FLEx tagging UI allows tags of DIFFERENT tag types to overlap the same words, but when a new tag of the SAME tag type (same top-level possibility, i.e. same 'row') overlaps existing tags, those existing tags are deleted; a tag's 'row' is the index of its top-level parent in the list.
findings.evidence: MakeTextTagInstance: 'ISet<ITextTag> overlappingTags = FindAllTagsReferencingOccurrenceList(SelectedWordforms); ... int tagRow = tagPoss.Owner.IndexInOwner; foreach (ITextTag overlappingTag in overlappingTags) { int overlappingTagRow = overlappingTag.TagRA.Owner.IndexInOwner; if (tagRow == overlappingTagRow) objsToDelete.Add(overlappingTag); } ... RootStText.TagsOC.Add(ttag); ttag.TagRA = tagPoss; ... DeleteTextTags(objsToDelete);'. Tests MakeTagAnnot_ExistTag_CompleteOverlap / FrontOverlap / RearOverlap / MultipleExistTags_Overlap create a second tag with a different possibility over the same words and assert the first was deleted.
findings.implication: Within one tag type ('Salience'), each word can carry at most one salience value as far as the FLEx UI is concerned - that matches 'one band per row'. If a user later tags overlapping words with any Salience sub-tag in FLEx, FDAT's tag is replaced (not corrupted). Keeping FDAT data in its own tag type avoids clashes with the user's RRG/Syntax tags.

findings.claim: A TextTag may span segment boundaries: GetOccurrences walks NextWordform() from the begin point to the end point across segments, skipping punctuation; IsValidRef only requires both segments/indices to exist and begin not after end. Tests create tags over occurrences {2,3,4} which are segment 0 index 2 and segment 1 indices 0-1.

IsValidRef: 'if (BeginSegmentRA == null || EndSegmentRA == null || ... BeginAnalysisIndex >= BeginSegmentRA.AnalysesRS.Count || EndAnalysisIndex >= EndSegmentRA.AnalysesRS.Count) return false; return !BegRef().IsAfter(EndRef());'. Test coords: '{ { 0, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, 2 }, { 1, 0 }, { 1, 1 }, ...' and 'new List<AnalysisOccurrence> { m_occurrences[2], m_occurrences[3], m_occurrences[4] }'.
findings.implication: A salience TextTag can cover a chart row whose words straddle a segment break (rows in FLEx charts are clause-based and can cross segments). However see the next finding for the 3+-segment limitation.

findings.claim: Multi-segment tag support is explicitly incomplete: tag lookup only checks BeginSegment or EndSegment (a tag spanning three or more segments is missed for its middle segments), and ChangeToDifferentIndex throws NotImplementedException when both endpoints of a multi-segment tag need adjusting.

'where segsUsed.Contains(ttag.BeginSegmentRA) || segsUsed.Contains(ttag.EndSegmentRA)'; and in TextTag.ChangeToDifferentIndex: 'if (fEnd && fBegin && BeginSegmentRA != EndSegmentRA) throw new NotImplementedException();'
findings.implication: If FDAT writes one TextTag per chart row and a row spans 3+ segments, the FLEx tagging view will not draw the tag on the middle segments and some baseline edits could hit a NotImplementedException path. Safer designs: one tag per (row, segment) fragment, or anchor to the row's first word only, or restrict to <=2 segments.

findings.claim: The FLEx tagging view renders a tag as the tag possibility's Abbreviation (best analysis WS) wrapped in localizable start/end bracket symbols, shown only on the first word of the span, on a separate line per top-level tag type (row index = possibility.Owner.IndexInOwner); no colour or style from the possibility is used.

Grep for ForeColor/BackColor/UnderColor in the Interlinear folder finds only 'BackColor = Color.FromKnownColor(KnownColor.Window)' (control background).
findings.implication: FDAT-created Salience tags will appear in FLEx's Texts > Tagging tab as e.g. '[S1 ... ]' under the words, on a 'Salience' line. Give each band possibility a short Abbreviation (that is what users will see) and a descriptive Name (shown in the right-click menu). Colours stored on the possibility are FDAT-only.

findings.claim: The tag list is LangProject.TextMarkupTags (owning atomic CmPossibilityList) with a strict two-level shape: top-level possibilities are 'tag types' (default: 'RRG Semantics', 'Syntax'), their SubPossibilities are the tags (ACTOR/ACT, Noun Phrase/NP ...). The right-click tag menu lists only top-level items that have sub-possibilities, one submenu per type.
findings.evidence: MasterLCModel: <owning num="55" id="TextMarkupTags" card="atomic" sig="CmPossibilityList">. MakeDefaultTextTags xml: '<possibility name="RRG Semantics"><subpossibility name="ACTOR" abbreviation="ACT"/>...'. MakeContextMenu_AvailableTags: 'foreach (ICmPossibility tagList in list.PossibilitiesOS) { if (tagList.SubPossibilitiesOS.Count > 0) AddListToMenu(menu, tagList); }' and AddListToMenu adds 'tagItem.Text = poss.Name.BestAnalysisAlternative.Text' for each sub-possibility.
findings.implication: An FDAT 'Salience' tag type must be a top-level CmPossibility in TextMarkupTags with the band values as its SubPossibilities. FDAT should create it with ICmPossibilityFactory under TextMarkupTagsOA.PossibilitiesOS (creating the list via GetDefaultTextTagList only if TextMarkupTagsOA is null, as the UI does at InterlinTaggingChild.cs:460-471).

findings.claim: FLEx's Lists-area tree handler enforces the two-level tag hierarchy on drag/drop: a tag type cannot be demoted, a tag cannot be promoted to the root, and nesting deeper than two levels is refused ('ksTagListTooDeep').
findings.evidence: 'if (m_objRepo.GetObject(hvoPossList).OwningFlid == LangProjectTags.kflidTextMarkupTags) return CheckAndReportBadTagListMove(...)' ... 'The moving item is a top-level Tag Type, it cannot be demoted. MessageBox.Show(m_tree, xWorksStrings.ksCantDemoteTagList ...' ... 'Can't promote tag to Tag Type root' ... '// This would give us hierarchy too deep (at least for now) MessageBox.Show(m_tree, xWorksStrings.ksTagListTooDeep'
findings.implication: FDAT must not nest salience bands more than one level below the 'Salience' type (e.g. no sub-bands); FLEx would treat deeper items as invalid moves and the tagging Vc only looks one level down.

findings.claim: CmPossibility.CanDelete is false when the possibility (or a sub-possibility) is referenced by any TextTag, when it is the only tag type in TextMarkupTags, or when IsProtected is true; the TextTag check applies ONLY to possibilities owned by the TextMarkupTags list.
findings.evidence: 'return base.CanDelete && !IsDefaultDiscourseTemplate && !IsThisOrDescendantInUseAsChartColumn && !IsOnlyTextMarkupTag && (OwningList != Cache.LangProject.TextMarkupTagsOA || !Services.GetInstance<ITextTagRepository>().GetByTextMarkupTag(this).Any()) && !IsProtected;' GetByTextMarkupTag: 'var tags = new HashSet<ICmPossibility> {tag}; tags.UnionWith(tag.SubPossibilitiesOS); return AllInstances().Where(ttag => tags.Contains(ttag.TagRA));'
findings.implication: Putting FDAT's salience values in TextMarkupTags means FLEx itself will refuse to let a colleague delete a band that is in use (and IsProtected=true blocks deletion even when unused). A custom list used only via FDAT-owned references would not get this TextTag protection.

findings.claim: IsProtected is documented as the flag for items 'accessed by the software via GUIDs'; when set the user can still edit the item but cannot delete it. Hidden is documented as controlling overlay bracketing only.
findings.evidence: <basic num="20" id="IsProtected" sig="Boolean"> 'This flag is set for items that are accessed by the software via GUIDs. The software is assuming that this item is always present with the same GUID on all machines. When set, a user can still edit the item, but it cannot be deleted.' <basic num="19" id="Hidden" sig="Boolean"> 'Indicates whether overlay bracketing should be hidden or not.'
findings.implication: FDAT should set IsProtected=true on the 'Salience' tag type and on any custom-list items it depends on by GUID. IsProtected and Hidden are hidden from the FLEx list editor (see completeFilter finding), so users cannot unset them accidentally.
