The citation itself is accurate: flexbridge/src/LibFLExBridge-ChorusPlugin/Infrastructure/FlexFolderSystem.cs:14-17 contains the quoted comment ("Exclude has precedence, but these are redundant as long as we're using the policy that we explicitly include all the files we understand") and lines 61-64 add IncludePatterns for LinkedFiles/AudioVisual/**.*, LinkedFiles/Others/**.*, LinkedFiles/Pictures/**.* and SupportingFiles/**.*. The include list is indeed explicit with no catch-all (lines 47-100), and it is applied at real Send/Receive time: SendReceiveActionHandler.cs:53-55 takes projectDir = directory of the .fwdata and passes FlexFolderSystem.ConfigureChorusProjectFolder into TriboroughBridgeUtilities.InitializeChorusSystem (TriboroughBridgeUtilities.cs:53-58), so the hg repo root is the FLEx project folder and <project>/LinkedFiles/Others is inside it. Chorus then runs `hg add -I <pattern>... -X <pattern>...` followed by commit (chorus HgRepository.cs:882-915, called from Synchronizer.cs:840-845). The implication that a new top-level FDAT folder would not be synced without a FLEx Bridge change is therefore SUPPORTED.

However, the claim as stated - "every file under LinkedFiles/Others, ... is included" - overstates the source and is contradicted by the same file and by Chorus:
1. Excludes take precedence, and the same method adds many of them (FlexFolderSystem.cs:18-45): **.xml, **.zip, **.bak, **.tmp, **.log, **.orig, **.flextext, **.fwbackup, **.fwstub, **.lint, **.oxes/oxesa/oxekt, *.fwdata/*.fwdb, plus ProjectFolderConfiguration.AddExcludedVideoExtensions (chorus ProjectFolderConfiguration.cs:68-98: mpa, mpe, mpg, mpeg, mpv2, mp2, mp4, mov, wmv, rm, avi, wvx, m1v). Chorus documents "NB: These take precedence over any includePatterns" (ProjectFolderConfiguration.cs:29-31). So e.g. an FDAT sidecar saved as .xml in LinkedFiles/Others would NOT sync. .json is not on any exclude list, so a JSON passes this filter.
2. Chorus's LargeFileFilter runs before every local commit (Synchronizer.cs:388-395: "the Send/Receive system can't handle large files. The following files won't be stored or shared"). It computes a per-extension maximum from the handlers' MaximumFileSize/GetExtensionsOfKnownTextFileTypes and falls back to 1 MB (Megabyte = 1,048,576) for any extension no handler claims (LargeFileFilter.cs:145-153, 155-178); oversized files are added to ExcludePatterns and, if already tracked, `hg forget`-ed (LargeFileFilter.cs:118-143). No handler claims "json": Chorus TextFileTypeHandler claims only "txt" (TextFileTypeHandler.cs:133-136), image and audio handlers get 10 MB (ImageFileTypeHandler.cs:84-86, AudioFileTypeHandler.cs:80-82), FLExBridge's FieldWorksCommonFileHandler reports only its strategy extensions such as "plsx" with int.MaxValue (FieldWorksCommonFileHandler.cs:199-204; ProjectLexiconSettingsStrategy.cs:111), and a grep of flexbridge src finds no "json" handler at all. INFERENCE: an FDAT JSON larger than 1 MB would be silently dropped from sync with only a progress warning.
3. On the FLEx side, Send/Receive first checks LinkedFilesLocationIsDefault() (FieldWorks Src/LexText/Lexicon/FLExBridgeListener.cs:291-308, 363-367) and shows the dialog "The Linked Files location for this project is not set to the default. This means that the linked files in this project will not be shared by Send/Receive." (Src/FwCoreDlgs/WarningNotUsingDefaultLinkedFilesLocation.resx:156, title at :295); the user may answer No and proceed. The default is <project>/LinkedFiles with subfolder "Others" (liblcm src/SIL.LCModel/LcmFileHelper.cs:39,45,106-108,153). So the JSON syncs only when LinkedFilesRootDir is the default.
4. Files with no handler fall to Chorus DefaultFileTypeHandler: CanValidateFile=false (DefaultFileTypeHandler.cs:33-36), so CommitCop never validates or rolls back a JSON (CommitCop.cs:59-80 validates only when handler.CanValidateFile), but Do3WayMerge cannot merge: it records an UnmergableFileTypeConflict and keeps "ours" under the WeWin mode FLExBridge/Chorus uses (DefaultFileTypeHandler.cs:42-59; Synchronizer.cs:830-835). INFERENCE for the FDAT design: concurrent edits to one JSON by two colleagues become a whole-file conflict, not a merge.
5. Minor: the pattern is **.* so a file with no extension would not match (inference from glob semantics; Chorus's own example "**.lift include all lift files, whereever they are found" at ProjectFolderConfiguration.cs:23 shows ** spans subdirectories, so subfolders of LinkedFiles/Others are included).

Net: the JSON-specific conclusion survives with conditions; the general "every file ... is included" statement does not.

(c) IsProjectLocked is a time-of-check probe: FieldWorks treats it as such and still catches the exception on open (FieldWorks/Src/Common/FieldWorks/FieldWorks.cs:2548-2560 up-front check; 3828-3835 "safety net for the narrow window where the project gets locked after ... up-front check"). Note also that the probe has side effects: it briefly writes the lock file and, if the existing lock is stale, deletes it (SimpleFileLock.ReleaseLock -> LockIO.DeleteLock).
(d) Stale-lock recovery requires the recorded PID to be dead OR its process name to differ (SimpleFileLock.cs:98-110); a reused PID belonging to another FieldWorks.exe would keep the lock alive. FDAT calling LCM directly (as flexlibs does) receives LcmFileLockedException itself; only FieldWorks.exe wraps it in StartupException (FieldWorks.cs:3120-3122).
